Title: His Dark Materials 3-Book Mass Market Paperback Boxed Set
How to Age Disgracefully
Review:
A great book to read if you want a fun, quick read. The characters all were interesting in different ways and I like all the different point of views.

Anyone who likes this book, I'd recommend All The Lonely People by Mike Gayle. Similar vibes, a great story. 

<spoiler>It's a bit stereotypical in that you know somehow of course the community center will be saved but it's still good. Like a sit com book, a bit over the top and unrealistic but everything always turns out OK, a light easy read. 
Also I wished Daphne and Art stayed purely friends, but I'm glad they're at least not in a proper relationship. 
I wish we had more about Art' s daughter, still not clear why she hates him so much. 
Loved Maggie the dog and the nativity play, very nice to see older people being inclusive with it too. 
Ziggy is great, nice to see a young single Dad rather than a Mum, plus him still going to university is great. </spoiler>

Title: Hope Street
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. I couldn't put it down, read through it one Saturday and it's getting me out of my reading slump which is always a good sign. 
I love the characters, especially Connor. I love how he's written and I was just routing for him the whole time.
The plot is interesting but for me it's more about the characters. Without spoilers, the his Mum part felt like it lingered in the background rather than actively playing a big part in the story aside from at the strat and the end. But I didn't mind that as focusing on everyone else was good for me. 
It made me happy, made me sad, overall a really good book that made me emotional in the best way. 
I found the ending with his Mum a little predictable, but it was still fine, just that bit didn't land as well compared to everything else in the book. 
Not quite a five star, I will say some of his other books I preferred that are give star, but still an amazing book.

Title: Sea of Souls
Review:
Another great book in the series.
I enjoyed the continued story of Toryn and Elodi. Without too many spoilers, I did enjoy this book but it is much more battle focused than character focused. For that reason I think I preferred book two, but this is a good solid entry in the series. 
I also like that we're now a the point where there isn't as much new info and we're building upon everything we've learnt so far, the world building is really starting to pay off. 
This book also has the best ending of the first three. It is a very satisfying ending, something I didn't feel for book one. It clearly finishes a story arc, yes there are still loose threads and plenty to carry on with, but it was a really good ending. 
I'll do more spoiler details, but overall I'm still loving this series! 
I will mention the stories are so linked, if you have a gap between reading them you may need to remind yourself. These books could really use a summary of the past book at the beginning, I've seen some series do it and this would benefit from it. 
<spoiler>I am still loving Elodi the Amayan! She's still my favourite character. I love how she talks the Lord into being a figurehead politician and that she should lead the battle, she's becoming good at the politics as well as embracing her heritage and her position. I want to see her with the other Amayans, we saw a brief bit at the end but I need more! 
Nyomae is good, it's been a while since book two so needed a refresher but I like her. 
Toryn is being Toryn, while nobody holds a candle to Elodi, he is a great character. Again need a refresher with his heritage as book one is a whole ago for me, but he's doing good learning everything in troubling times. A mix of using the song and fighting and he's improving loads at both. 
The spiders are creepy as hell, just had to mention it. I hate spiders and yikes! The battle at the end is a great ending. You feel they should win as it is book three, but they're so overwhelmed. I do like that we know a lot of the plan, with Dorlan and the Amayans, as it doesn't come across as a Deux Ex Machina, they win due to their good strategy despite coming from a weak position. Overall, great book, looking forward to the next one! </spoiler>

Title: Before the Coffee Gets Cold
Review:
A nice cosy book to get into. I needed a shortish and easy book to get me out of my recent reading slump and this definitely fit the bill. 
The cafe is interesting and so are all the staff and various people that come and visit it. 
You don't get too much information on each person, it's more like snippets, but I like what we do learn about each character. I'll leave a spoiler below about one issue I really didn't like but the rest was good. 
Overall a good book, don't expect any information on how anything works, it's more of a just go with it and enjoy the ride kind of book. 
<spoiler>I hate the last story, women giving birth knowing they will die frustrates me to no end. I wish more stories would be less anti abortion especially in these cases. It felt very propaganda-like having the child saying she was glad she was born. </spoiler>

Title: Beach Read
Review:
I don't read a lot of romance and I liked this more than I thought I would.
Whilst it is a romance at heart, it has enough else going on especially with following the research for Gus' story. 
I was rooting for the characters the entire book, they weren't perfect but I liked them because of it. 
I also appreciate there wasn't too much of the miscommunication trope (there was a little) as that often bugs me when everything could be solved with a conversation. 
More thoughts below but overall I really enjoyed it. 
<spoiler>This book felt like it was exploring different kinds of people, from talking about cults to family dynamics, it wasn't all romance which is what I like about it. 
The side characters were good but not as in depth as I would have liked. I wish we'd seen her friend and Mum a bit more especially. Love Pete & Maggie, again would have liked to have seen more of them, they seem to have the healthiest relationship in the whole book. Maybe that's less interesting but I would have enjoyed learning more about them.</spoiler>

Title: Cross the Line
Review:
It is a fine light hearted romance novel. I don't usually read romance but thought I would try it, so an F1 based one seemed like a good idea as I know about the sport and thought it would add to the book.

<spoiler>
Not a criticism of the book exactly, but for me there wasn't enough about the plot and it felt a bit shallow at times. You need either character development or a good plot in my opinion and this was lacking in both a bit. I know the main thing is romance, but given they liked each other from the start and nothing really got in their way it felt a little bland. Also I could do without the sex scenes, but as someone who doesn't read romance much I know that's just my opinion and I'm not really the target audience for this. 
Overall I thought it was a fine book, nothing too bad but nothing amazing either. It's a nice easy read when you don't want anything heavy, just a fun romance book.</spoiler>

Title: Wolfsong
Review:
I wanted to read this as I have loved other books by TJ Klune. 
This doesn't live up to the likes of House on the Cerulean Sea and others for me. 
At first it felt like Twilight fanfic or Twilight inspired, there clearly are going to be werewolves. The Bennett family also gave me Cullen vibes, creepy, keep to themselves, randomly arrive in village. The guys at the shop Ox works at remind me of the Black family too. Plus the setting, it really feels inspired by Twilight which detracted from it for me (and I enjoyed Twilight books 1-3 for reference). 
It feels like this book is written in a very young adult style, which is fine, but odd given where the romance is going. I felt like I was reading something for a twelve year old (and I do like YA sometimes so it's not necessarily a negative), but given the content and where it seems to be going it seems really mismatched to me. 
Also a side note, calling a character Elizabeth Bennett seems like a bizarre choice, it doesn't seem to be for any reason and it's a really specific name from one of the most famous books ever. Maybe it pays off later, but still. 
I can tell this is going to be a romance and starting with a weird age gap (10 to 16) is not a great look, even if they only get together later. Could they not have made Joe older?
Plus it just feels to me like the entire Bennett family is very cult like and I get the impression I'm supposed to like them but the way they treat Ox, like he's supposed to cure their kid, and the way they act with others makes me really not like the entire family.
This is the main reason I'm not going to finish this, I feel like the rest of the book is going to revolve around me supposed to be rooting for them and I just can't, I want them to leave Ox alone.
There are so many other good books in the world, I'm not wasting time on this. 
I still like TJ Klune's other work, but it's clear this series isn't for me.

Title: Dimension Quest
Review:
Given the end of the previous book and the title I had high expectations and was expecting this to be the last book in the series.
I really like this entry, the first without a new main character and it switches points of view throughout, it's done really well. 
I always root for the Protectors and was hoping they'd get together and defeat Evil the entire book, of course it is never that simple. I liked the different complications, Hesperides is a great too, love her introduction. 
No spoilers here, if you've enjoyed the series at all so far you should read this. It is one of if not the best book in the entire series.

Title: Harry, a History: The True Story of a Boy Wizard, His Fans, and Life Inside the Harry Potter Phenomenon
Rebellion Quest
Review:
Another quest book to enjoy! This one feels a bit different from the others which I like.
Janet is an interesting character to follow and I like her journey. Also without being too spoilery it is definitely a quest that tells you more about the wider universe as well as tying in things from past books which I always like. 
Only a small spoiler as it's very soon in the book - <spoiler>I liked seeing a counterpart switch as it's been a while. Also interesting how different Janol and Janet are whilst Galar and Galen seem much more similar. Good thing Janet got to the tree first as I don't know how effective Janol would have been at guiding Galen!</spoiler>
The ending of this book is something. Definitely something. Without giving anything away, first one of the series that really makes you want it read on.

Title: Malory Towers: New Term: Book 7
Authors: Pamela Cox, Pamela Cox, Enid Blyton

Title: Orbital
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. Despite there being no real plot or character development, I was hooked.
It's more like the earth is a character and we see it from different points of view, at different times and in very different ways.
We get a few views from the surface but mostly it's from the spaceship and the writing is really well done. I didn't realise there were that many ways to describe moving across the earth, but apparently there are and it's done very well. The prose is the strongest part of this book by far. 
This book also just makes you think and reflect on life in general, it puts you in the shoes of someone on the space station, where you feel so small compared to the world and the universe. 
Overall, loved it!

Title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
Didikai Witch
Review:
I really enjoyed this book!
I wasn't sure what to expect when I started but I couldn't put it down and had to know what happens next.
I was really invested in all the characters and it does a really good job at showing why characters do certain things and showing different points of view.
The world building is also great, it's well done without being too much like an information dump and I want to know more about it. 
While it's the first book in a series, it's got a good satisfying arc in itself, with some interesting hints to the next book but without suffering from first book syndrome which is a really good writing. Loved that! 
The last thing before getting into spoilers, definitely need to continue this series! 
<spoiler>At the start of the book I was getting major cult vibes from the coven and glad we switched to The Beyond aka the real world. 
It reminds me a bit of Buffy but with grown ups, in the best way possible. 
The Daryavaush chapters are some of the best, I liked them more than Amethyst and when we switched over for a bit at chapter twelve was when the book really got good for me.
Also love the twists that aren't too out there but still you don't see. Alex and Carla and Nikita are all great, kinda saw Alex coming a bit but really not the other one so was super shocked, but in a good way. 
Also the other supernaturals and the thing with the amulet that are probably going to be more important in the future books are a good way to seed the next book without it being an annoying cliffhanger.</spoiler>

Title: The Priory of the Orange Tree
A Visit From the Goon Squad
Worm
Moods: adventurous, challenging, dark, emotional, mysterious, sad, tense

Title: The Second Form at St Clare's
The Midnight Train
Review:
I absolutely loved this book. Even better than The Midnight Library. Wilbur is a great character and his life is a really interesting one to follow. It's the right balance of being relatable, a little much but in a way that can easily happen to people.
I like the train, the direction the story takes and the ending itself. The journey is the best part, as is often the case will these books. 
It is the kind of book that makes you think about your life, what you value and what you want. I can't remember the exact quote, but something along the lines of your present life is your future nostalgia, which really hit hard for me. 
More thoughts in spoilers, but loved it and would recommend it. 
<spoiler>The Dreamer coming on was a great twist and one I really liked. So many Wilburs! Having both definitely added to some of the stops.
The Dreamer changing from not understanding and learning throughout the journey and going on to live a better life is great. 
I kind of wish I knew if Wilbur did make it into eternity or what happened at the end, but maybe that's for a future book! Same as Nora here, a great feature from her. </spoiler>

Title: Parsnips, Buttered
Review:
This is a nice fun and funny read. Nothing groundbreaking but it is good comedy and I enjoyed reading it. 
Knocked off a bit mostly because I don't think some bits have aged well, references to things like Twitter and other things just don't hit as much. Also a few of the bits I felt were teetering from being funny to slightly mean, especially when some things were directed at clearly employees who had no say on company policies. 
It definitely reads as Joe Lycett, I can hear him saying everything, which is always a plus. 
Overall though I got a few laughs, it's easy to read in small bits here and there and I'm glad I read it.

Title: I Who Have Never Known Men
The Woman in Me
Review:
It's not the easiest read but it's well worth it. I am so glad I read this book, some parts about the conservatorship are so sad and can be hard to listen to, but it's important to know how awful some of the systems in our world are if we have any hope of improving them, so I'm glad Britney Spears took the time to write this. 
Only slight thing I wasn't such a fan of was a lot of the religious mentions towards the end. I know it is her life but as someone not religious it's odd hearing how God helped her, when God seemingly didn't for most of her life. 
There could have been more of some of her early life, it definitely is a bit pick and choose with random bite if her life but that ties into the style which is more conversational. It's written more like she's telling you about her life in a conversation than a thorough detailed biography. 
Would definitely recommend it. 
The audiobook is well read too, Britney Spears does the introduction and Michelle Williams narrates the rest, all of it is great and I would recommend it as an audiobook.

Title: The Sixth Form at St. Clare's
As Good As Dead
Contributors: Clare Corbett (Narrator), Kristin Atherton (Narrator), Jot Davies (Narrator), Maryam Grace (Narrator), Luke Poli (Narrator)
Review:
I have such mixed feelings about this book. Giving it a 3 star is an average, as it's like half a 4 star half a 2 star for me. 
I like following the case, the first half of the story goes well with the trilogy. Still think the first book is best though. 
I'll do spoilers at the end, can't say anything else really about the second part without spoilers. 
I'd still recommend it especially if you like the first two books. Was just disappointed in the end. 
Spoilers now! <spoiler>The second part of the book I just didn't like. I wish the police had caught her tied up in duct tape and then caught Jason. No need for the whole cover up story. Also as an aside as soon as she read the email from Andy I was sure it was him and I feel like Pip should have known too, she's smart, she should have picked up on it. 
I just didn't like the whole murder and frame plot. Yes it sucks Max got off but that's unfortunately far too common. I wish they caught Jason fair and square instead. Plus it felt so long and drawn out. I ended up semi spoiling the ending reading reviews as I was getting antsy I just needed the answer and it was dragging so much. </spoiler>

Title: Invisible Women: Exposing Data Bias in a World Designed for Men
Review:
It was a really interesting book, but a bit depressing to read so took me a while. Learning about all the ways women get treated badly isn't a fun subject but it's worth reading. It is a little dry, I'm glad I listened to it on audio as I would have struggled more with a physical book. 
I knew a lot of it anyway but some things were new to me so I'm really glad I read it. 
My only complaints are I think it could have been written in a way that was a bit more engaging as I put it down multiple times, I wasn't longing to continue it. It is so information dense, and I know it's non fiction, but it could have been written in a different way somehow to be a better read. 
Also the book mainly focuses on western experiences (Northern America and Europe), which is fine but women often have different experiences around the world. It does touch on other countries sometimes, but it does primarily refer to western countries. There isn't really any intersectionality here either, no mention of trans women, women of different races, LGBTQ, neurodiverse, etc., which would have been appreciated.

Title: Heartstopper Volume 1
Review:
I'm not usually one for graphic novels but I really enjoyed reading this.
Good LGBTQ representation, the art was great, a really fun read. Also as a Brit it's great to read things set here, makes me nostalgic about my school days! 
Need to get the next few books now!

Title: Project Hail Mary
Review:
I loved this book! Another great story from Andy Weir. 
I like the premise of it, and the flashbacks as he is remembering pieces of his past is really interesting. 
It's hard to make too many comments without spoiling it, though I love Stratt as a character, she is great. Also the scientists in general ignoring politics is good. 
My only real complaint is it is extremely similar to The Martian, so if you have read it, it can seem repetitive. The main characters are ridiculously similar too, it could be the same guy. 
Also whilst I really enjoy it, I am somewhat science-y, I could see someone who isn't as science-y may not enjoy some of the details. You could skim over them and it won't affect the plot, but just a heads up as it does play a big part in some sections of the book. 
<spoiler>I love Rocky, he is the best, I'm so glad he didn't die and got to save Erid. Love it! 
I really like them working together. I do wonder if any data on them was sent back with the beetles, as Grace never made it back. 
I was a bit sad he didn't get to return to earth at the end, but at least he didn't die!
I figured there would be a happy ending, as with the Martian, even more similarities there. Definitely a lot of similar plot beats in the way it's structured. It's fine for a this but I'm not sure how many of these books Weir can do before it starts to seem a bit repetitive. </spoiler>

Title: What You Are Looking For is in the Library
Review:
I really enjoyed reading this book. It's easy to get into and be sucked into, but also perfect as you can easily read a chapter a day.
Overall I really enjoyed this book and would definitely recommend it. 

<spoiler>I liked following each character and their journeys and how they all used the library. It was also nice to see side characters pop up in each other's stories, especially later in when they hint and resolving some things from earlier chapters. 
All the chapters end in a very open ended way, some may not like that but I think it works very well here. 
My only slight dislike is how the librarian is described, it's a bit repetitive and I don't know why there needs to be an emphasis on her being a large women who likes cookies, it felt a bit unnecessary.</spoiler>

Title: Dawn
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. 
The alien species are a standout for me, they're so well done and feel so alien and not just a deviation of humans. 
The plot was interesting, I spent the entire book unsure of the Oankali and changing my mind constantly about them. I was having to stop myself from reading too quickly as I was desperate to know what happened. 
Will definitely continue the series, but I may need a bit of a break as it's a heavy book for sure. 
<spoiler>I'm not a massive fan of rape and sexual assault in books. I think it is handled well here, though because of the alien nature I wasn't even sure it was rape initially. Even so, it's just not for me. Was the only part of the book I didn't like though. 
Generally the end and realising what the Oankali are doing is horrifying. I saw someone say the Oankali treat humans like we do endangered animals, which isn't a perfect comparison but it's not far off. We don't interfere as much, but also I don't think humans treat animals that well a lot either so it kind of parallels.</spoiler>
Content Warnings: Graphic: Rape, Sexual assault, Sexual violence; Minor: Suicidal thoughts;

Title: Barrier Quest
Review:
One if my favourite books in the series. Ben is a great character, I love learning about him and following him on this journey.
Without being too spoilery I like that this book gives us more insight into the grid system as a whole. The first two mostly focus just on the Land, here we get more which I really appreciate. 
I could do with a bit less lust from Ben at points, but I'll overlook that for the rest of the book which I love.

Title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
The Honjin Murders
Review:
This was an interesting murder mystery novel. I've read one of the other books later in the series and liked it so thought I'd come back and start from the beginning.
It's a good story, it's easy to read and it's a good balance of being not too predictable or too unbelievable. I've read a few Japanese books but only one mystery and I liked it and will continue to read the rest of the series.
It's not necessarily ground breaking, but it's a good read and I'd recommend it.

Title: If on a Winter's Night a Traveler
Review:
This is a very bizarre book. Experimental, very meta, it is an odd book to read. You need to be in a very specific frame of mind to finish it.

The writing is very well done which is what brings it up for me, but if it wasn't so well written I would have rated it lower. The writing could have been toned down a bit too, just because you can doesn't mean you need to in every sentence. It felt like the author was trying to showcase their writing ability, which are clearly is very good, but it made it difficult to read at points and hard to get through. I couldn't read too much in one sitting, I had to put it down and return to it a day or two later.

In addition I was getting confused about the characters towards the end as I read this over a period of time and couldn't remember some of the previous bits. I think it would be a good book for rereads if you enjoy it, but I can't face reading it again, once was enough. 

Also I think reading this as a woman is less enjoyable. Every single male character, in any chapter or story, seems to heavily objectify women which is very off-putting. Plus when they when are trying to immerse you as the reader, male pronouns are used. As someone not using male pronouns, this part of the book I don't think had the intended impact as I couldn't put myself in the position of the reader.

Title: Fun and Games at Malory Towers
Assistant to the Villain
Review:
It reads so juvenile, yet the characters are supposed to be adults.
She actually said you're too pretty to be evil and kept thinking don't fall in love with the bad guy. 
Also he's called the villain with no name is bizarre. 
Mostly though the writing is not great, romance seems awful already and too childish. I like some young adult but this seems even younger, or maybe it's just the bad writing.

Title: Zami: A New Spelling of My Name
Evenings and Weekends
Review:
I had mixed feelings about this book, but I enjoyed it more as I continued to read it.
It's told from so many different perspectives, which are a bit confusing at first as there are just so many and they don't that have distinct voices, but I got the hang of it. 
I liked some characters more than others. Rosaleen was the best by far for me, she was the only character I was really invested in. 
I wanted to know what would happen with some of the drama between the others, but I didn't feel that emotionally invested most of them. They all have flaws and most of them don't seem like they're doing much to overcome them, it's hard care about them when they don't even care about each other half the time. 
More spoilers below, but I think this book handled some difficult topics really well. It is great for gay male representation especially, though to the extent that the opposite sex couple is written oddly more in spoilers below. It's also very male dominated which I could have had less of. 
I like the whale concept, I wish they did more with it though. I wanted more from Valerie the reporter.
This book reminds me a bit of Normal People, though I did prefer this as I really liked Rosaleen's story. I found Normal People OK, but I know some people love it and I'd recommend this to people who liked it as it's got similar vibes. 
<spoiler>A few spoiler notes, the sex scene reads as very man writing women with Ed & Maggie at the start, they had good sex and came at the same time, really? I hate unrealistic sex scenes like that, really wish authors would stop it as it feels lazy. Especially as the rest of the sexual stuff in the book is so much better. Feels like the author didn't want to write a positive opposite sex scene. 
On a better note, how they handled Phil's rape was really well done I thought. Also the topic of abortion again a hard one but written very well. 
I also appreciate talking about Irish history, Pauline's story, talking about how women were treated, again done well. </spoiler>

Title: Army Without Banners
Review:
This was a really interesting book, I'm very glad I read it. It's a slice of live book following one main woman, Mildred Gibson, as she moves to London out of guilt to help out as an ambulance driver during the blitz. I've not read much on this topic, I'm not sure how much there is on the civilian side during the second world war, but I'd be interested to read more like this, especially following women as the wars did a lot to change where they were allowed to work.
The writing was good and I also liked having the drawings throughout, they're small sketches but they add to the day-to-day feeling of the book, that you're just following regular people going about lives. They're not extraordinary, just regular people doing their best work, but together they accomplish amazing feats like so many did throughout the war.
There is a bit of an arc from her being an outsider to becoming one of them, but it is mostly stories of different raids and other days during the war - not always the busiest days, but they all have something of note and something different which I like. It's more like reading a handful of diary entries, but not every day, only a select few. I particularly enjoyed when she visits the hospital with the librarian and the river group. It shows how so many people are just doing their bit and that everything matters in it's own way and is important. 
I also think these kind of books are important in general, as we're getting to the point in history where almost nobody alive will remember the war and we should make sure these books are available so we can learn from history and not repeat it.
This is my second book by the author and I'm definitely up for reading more.

Title: The Bear and the Nightingale
Review:
Overall I enjoyed reading this book. It was a bit slow at the start and I was worried I wouldn't like it as much, but it really picked up towards the end and I liked it more and more as I read it. Will definitely have to read the rest of the trilogy now. 
I like the ties to folklore and despite words and names being of a Russian origin it was still easy to follow and not mix people up. 
I like the main character Vasya, I think it was slow at the start with more backstory and before she's introduced, I was really invested in her story and what was going to happen to her personally as well as the broader plot. 
It being slow at the start and a couple of minor things below stop it from being a five star, still is a good book though. 
<spoiler>A few spoiler thoughts here now. Konstantin is awful, written well for me to dislike him so much. Very well done.
I feel a bit odd about women being treated like property and how they're supposed to want to be married. I know Vasya is different but surely non magical people could want a better life too, I wish maybe one of her sisters had the same feelings. Lots of women don't want that life. A bit annoying.
Also casual mentions of men raping their wives, or taking them to bed as they say, seemed a bit off. Unnecessary maybe? I know it may be one of those things of the time, but it makes me dislike Pyotr so much, probably more so than intended. It was often just throwaway lines, so it didn't really add to the story either. 
I was happy with the ending, it feels like it could be a standalone book which is nice, though I do want to read more. Free Vasya sounds interesting to follow, I wonder what she'll get up to. 
 </spoiler>

Title: Song of Echoes
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. Wasn't sure what to expect but I am glad I read it.
The world building is great, maybe too much of it in some places but it is the first book so it's to be expected. The map at the front of the book is really helpful, I wish more books did this. Glad I got a physical copy when I got the first two books in person. 
I really liked following Toryn and Elodi, especially Elodi, she's a really well written woman which is far too uncommon in fantasy and her story is interesting. 
Love Elodi, no notes, I want more of her story and hope she continues to play a major role. 
Toryn was good too, I liked Hamar's stories more than his, details in spoilers below. 
My minor complaints with this book are far too many chapters end in a cliff hanger prior to switching perspective, it felt unnecessary, I wanted to carry on reading and change at a more natural point. 
Also the ending, more details in the spoilers, not that it's bad but it felt like an odd place to end it. 
Overall still really enjoyed it though and will definitely be reading the rest of the series. 
<spoiler>I wish we learnt more about Toryn, I felt like there is so much left to know about his heritage and it felt like his sections were about the people and world around him more than him. Which is great for learning about Hamar and the world, but I wanted more - I'm hoping we'll find out in future books. 
For the ending, it barely felt like an ending especially for Toryn. At least Elodi had a battle with a resolution. Toryn has spent far too much time wondering and not achieving a lot, then it literally ends with him approaching the city. I needed some sort of resolution, I enjoyed his story but it wasn't an end, which is frustrating to me.</spoiler>

Title: The Callista Ascendancy
Review:
I was given a free copy in exchange for a review. 

Another great entry to the Natural Human Saga. I was glad to come back to Kali, and whilst it does take a bit to get back into the story, once you are you're hooked and I couldn't put it down. 
I like how the different perspectives are handled, you can always tell who you're following without needing to spell it out and it flows nicely. 
I like the overall story, this one is even more politics than the previous one but I like that about it. 
The second half is especially compelling, more details in the spoiler below as to why. 
Overall, I enjoyed it and will continue to read any further books in this series. 


<spoiler>To me the Decca plot and finding the other human ship was my favourite part of the book. I was so invested in that court case, love how Kali solved it in the end. 
So sad that Toklo died, I was really hoping he was going to be a character in future series. I'm curious about his sky blade though, it seems that may be important somehow. Also it's a shame to see Torsta going away, though I'm sure there will be a way to bring her back somehow, maybe she does help the humans find their home! 
Not as much progress in the Free Republic and with Alka as I'd hoped, I guess that's for the next book! 
Wasn't expecting a snippit of the next book at the end, but I'm holding off until release as I don't want to spoilt myself. </spoiler>

Title: Wicked: The Life and Times of the Wicked Witch of the West
Review:
I had a good time reading this book. It was a bit hard to get into at first and it is very different to the musical so don't expect anything remotely similar to it. 
I liked the story, I enjoyed following the characters and learning about Oz. 
It's definitely a book I had to be in the mood to read, but I binged it over two sittings as once I started I didn't want to put it down. 
I liked this book but didn't love it, which is why I knocked off a star. I want to continue the series as I did really enjoy it. 
<spoiler>I liked that the characters are older meaning themes along politics, religion, relationships, etc. all are much more in depth and mature which I wasn't expecting and was pleasantly surprised by. 
I enjoyed the backstory but especially the years at Shiz in the Emerald City were some of the most interesting parts to me. I liked her in the Vinkus too where she stayed with Fiyero's family.
It can be a bit much sometimes as it feels like there is too much information and a lot of characters so it can be overwhelming. You can miss crucial things so easily as there is a lot going on, I often would double back to read bits as a character can die in an off comment and you may not fully clock it at first. It can be like that at times so if you're a fast reader you often need to either slow down or reread bits. 
I hope the future books will be easier in this regard though as some of the world and people won't need to be introduced and explained as much. 
I like how it ties in Dorothy, I didn't know she featured at all and I liked her at the end of it. 
</spoiler>

Title: Girls in Love
Review:
Rereading some old childhood books and it's a fun easy read.
It's definitely aimed at teens and it does it well, giving me flashbacks of when I was younger and the problems you face that seem like the end of the world.

Title: The Murder After the Night Before
Review:
I enjoyed this book, I'm not usually into thrillers, but this felt like more of a mystery than a thriller. So maybe not one for thriller fans, but a good read none the less.
It felt very lighthearted in an odd way, despite the book being about a murder it's following the life of the main character and isn't all that dark, a pleasant surprise. 
Very addictive to read too, I was racing through the end to find out what happened. 
It's a good book to read, it's not a masterpiece or anything, but it's fun. 
<spoiler>
One thing I wasn't happy about was the ending just jumped on you with the answer, the characters never found out, it felt a bit jarring. You felt no connection to Posey as you've not followed her, suddenly in the last chapter you see from her POV but I didn't care for her at all so it didn't hit as much. I think the last bit could have been done differently as it wasn't the best ending in my opinion. </spoiler>

Title: 10 Minutes 38 Seconds in This Strange World
Becoming
Review:
I did enjoy this book, but it is a bit on the long side so took me a while to finish. I listened to the audiobook which she narrates herself, definitely a good narrator and would recommend listening to it over reading it physically. 
I listened to this after Barack Obama's book which probably isn't ideal as I really enjoyed that was expecting this to be more similar so it set up incorrect expectations. 
I find the politics, life in the white house and everything a really helpful insight to counter Barack's memoir. I could have done a bit less with the family life, a bit was interesting but there was too much of it, especially as they put so much effort into keeping their kids away from the limelight it felt odd to have them feature so much in this. 
It's odd this book actually made me like Barack a bit less, whilst he was a great president it sounds like he wasn't a great husband or father, and no doubt Michelle is being more generous rather than less. 
I did enjoy this book, but it wasn't what I was expecting. I put it down for ages and came back to it months later as it felt so long. Not a bad book, but not as good as I had hoped for as I had high expectations.

Title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
In the Fifth at Malory Towers
Age of Shadows
Review:
A great sequel in the series. I really enjoyed following Toryn and Elodi again throughout their stories. This time I was more equally engaged in both stories, before I was more interested in Elodi but this book restored my interest in Toryn too.
The pacing was good, the world building is paying off more and little bits are being added but it builds on the first book naturally, so feels less world building heavy. I didn't have to go back and check things as much this time.
Without spoilers, I'll say I enjoyed the plot and I think the ending of this book is more satisfying than the first and feels like a good ending, whilst also leaving the door open and showing the direction the next book will take. It feels like the end of an arc, whereas I felt a bit more left hanging in the first book. 
One gripe is that the author still has the habit of leaving so many chapters ending in a cliff hanger before switching viewpoints, which feels unnecessary a lot of the time. 
Great book overall and look forward to the rest of the series. This book for me is better than the first, hoping it carries on up and up!
Spoiler thoughts below. 
<spoiler>I like this story building up to the opening and then not-opening of the gate, it felt like a story in itself whilst still being a wider part of the series. 
I really enjoyed learning about the Amayans and Nym in the forest, that section was one of my favourites. Losing Calerdon was one of the sadest things, it was so well written and I felt so much for Elodi, I couldn't believe it either. I really hope they get it back!
I was feeling something off about the Archon but I couldn't place it and I was really glad with the reveal. It was a twist enough to throw you, but also it makes perfect sense with everything so far. Glad the awful Vice is gone too, they were just mean as a human rather than being possessed.
It's nice that Toryn and Elodi met at the end, though I'm curious how the next books will be, if they'll split up and we'll get alternating chapters again or if it will be something different. I'm not sure how I feel about them being together, there definitely seems to be something there but I was kind of hoping there wouldn't be as I don't like how main characters often get coupled up. My mind may change on this so we shall see. </spoiler>

Title: Hunt Quest
Review:
Another great entry to the series. It's nice to have another guy main character as it's been a while. Another flirt just like Ben, but I prefer Zach as it's more playful and less awkward.
Similar to the last book, it felt like he knew much more of what he was getting into. Not in knowing the Land but in the quest, less unknowns, which is an interesting way the series may be going. 
Overall I really enjoyed this book, looking forward to carrying on with the series now.

Title: An Anthology of New Feminist Translations
Review:
I find it hard to rate and review this collection. It's an anthology of translations, but of the five four if them are excerpts of stories rather than complete, which does make it hard to follow in some places. It's like I'm reading a teaser for a full length book. I would have preferred if they had kept to short stories or short essays, it would have been easier to follow - especially as a couple of the stories are already somewhat tricky to read by nature as they are not just translated but in some cases are older texts with very different styles. Some of it definitely went over my head as someone who doesn't know a lot of the history. 
I did enjoy reading all of them, the theatre one was my favourite and was the one that felt like a full story in itself. The bed sheet one was also really good and it did work well without having the full context as it's more a slice of life anyway. 
It is definitely not something I would usually read and I am glad I read it.

Title: A Story for Every Day of Summer
Review:
It's hard to rate as all the stories are different. Some better than others. I ended up taking a break then rushing through the end of these, but that's more to me having other books on the go rather than these not being as good. 
Still enjoyed them, reading slightly out of order as I started with winter but definitely want to read the autumn ones now.

Title: The Bluest Eye
Review:
I have mixed thoughts on this book, but in general I am glad I read it. I would hesitate to say I enjoyed it though, given everything that goes on. 
The book is very well written. It is giving backstory to each character, though the constant changes of narrators is a bit confusing. To me the seasons didn't make much sense either, maybe I'm missing it but given how time was so flexible the seasons grouping was basically forgettable. 
It's interesting for a book about Pecola to have so little from her. I also wish we heard more from Freida and Claudia. I really liked them at the start and was sad we didn't stay with them. Especially given I disliked a lot of the other perspectives. For me personally, I have no interest in trying to learn the backstory of pedophiles and rapists. I do think those chapters fell a bit short. They came across as awful people all the time, I learnt nothing new about them and would have rather got the information needed for the story from someone else. 
Overall it's a well written book, but I didn't like it as much as everyone else seems to.

Title: After I Do
Review:
I mostly enjoyed this book, it was an easy read and I enjoyed learning about the different characters and the family dynamics.

<spoiler>
I wish Lauren grew more as a person over the year, I felt she didn't really learn much about herself.
Aldo everything between her and Ryan seemed unhealthy and I was hoping they wouldn't get together, then they did without really much of a reason. I didn't like the whole you need to just never give up on marriage attitude it portrayed, for both Lauren and her brother. 
It seemed like trying to wrap up multiple unhealthy relationships in marriages at the end, plus the trope of a baby being born whilst the grandmother died seemed pointless and forced.
I was hoping for more complexity instead of trying to tie everything up neatly at the end. </spoiler>

I read TJRs other book Daisy Jones & The Six before this which I loved, it's a shame to me this one was nowhere near as good. That was amazing, this was fine/good.

Title: The Tales of Beedle the Bard
Business as Usual
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. It's not something I would usually pick up but I found it really interesting. I've been enjoying interesting formats recently and I like the letters that are being used here.
<spoiler>It's nice to follow a women in the 1930s and read what day to day life was like. It's interesting that having a degree is bad, and the ways woman are treated. Especially how life revolves around marriage and it's seen as unusual for a woman of her class to work as she doesn't need to - the other women working all seem to do so because they have to. 
I really liked reading this book, for an older book it is surprising easy to read I found. I would definitely recommend it. </spoiler>

Title: The Shetland Witch: Or, Atropos Wants Her Shears Back
Review:
It was really interesting to read, I really enjoyed this book. It takes a bit of time to get into the swing the dialog at first as it's written with the accent, but I got used to it fairly quickly - anyone unfamiliar with a Scottish accent may find it difficult though. 
<spoiler>
Overall I liked the mix of mythology, I am unfamiliar with it so can't comment on too much, but I enjoyed how it all played out.
The plot is good and strong throughout the story, aside from the pregnancy which I'm still not sure who the father was as I couldn't figure it out. 
I wish there was more character development, I liked what was there but there coukd have been more, not just for the main character but others too. It was hoping for more of the sisterhood - I liked what was there but I wish there was more! 
I did really enjoy this story as a sole though, 4/5.</spoiler>

Title: An Echo of Things to Come
Review:
I really enjoyed this, not as much as the first book but still a really good read.
I liked continuing to follow the story of Asha, Torin, Davian and Caeden throughout the book, though I definitely cared about some stories more than others. Caeden's especially seemed a bit unrelated to others for a lot of the book and a bit more disjointed, still interesting though.
I still love Asha the entire time, more on that in the spoilers below though.
I did loose track of some things occasionally, part of me feels like I need to read a summary of the book again as it's so dense. And that's despite me reading the book fairly quickly, if I'd read it over a long period of time I'm sure I'd forget some bits of it.
The ending didn't feel as satisfying as I wanted as it still left so much hanging. It didn't feel like a true ending in a way, barely anything was resolved and it's definitely setting up for the final book. 
Despite me complaining about some things I really am loving this series. It's great they have a summary at the start as I needed it this time and definitely will for the next one too. Only one book to go now! 

<spoiler>So happy Asha got un-shadowed and so sad about her in the end. I really hope in the last book she isn't just stuck in the tributary, I want to see more of her.
I lost track a bit of Caeden sometimes, as despite the summary there is just so much happening you can easily forget who the Lyth are or what exactly he's up to. 
Kind of sad about Brashada but I the Nethgalla story worked really well and whilst for the characters I hope she goes away, I'm curious to see what happens with her now. Her being the Shadraehin too was surprising in the best way. 
A bit more on the ending, apart from Torin probably staying as Northwarden and the boundary kind of closing, it felt like the characters stories didn't resolve much at all, I know the boundary did but I care more about the characters!</spoiler

Title: A Story For Every Day of Autumn
Review:
Some good stories, the quality does vary as it is from a group of authors. Some are absolutely amazing, some are just OK. One was very confusing. Glad I read it though.
A good way to get back into reading if you don't read a lot as most days are only a page or two.

Title: Never Lie
Review:
It's a really interesting book and I'm glad I read it. A really quick read which was nice. Nothing great but it wasn't terrible either. It had potential to be much better as the premise was good but it could have been done better I think. 
<spoiler>I disliked basically every single character in it from the outset. I was worried I would be supposed to like them but turns out I was right! I was worried EJ meant Ethan, but it seemed too obvious so I'm glad it wasn't. 
I expected some of the twists bit not all of them which was good balance of it not being too out of left field but still being interesting.
What I thought was odd is going back to earlier in the book some of it really contradicts itself once you know the twist which made me like it less. The more I went back over it the more inconsistentit seemed.</spoiler>

Title: Think Again
Review:
It's a good follow on from the kids books, though it does read weirdly young in parts. The character is supposed to be 40 and it could be a bit more adult. Maybe Ellie is just supposed to be really immature, but it seemed off.
Also not enough Nadine and Magda, the books were focused on all three of them but this is very much an Ellie story. 
They also changed the name of a character for no reason which was confusing at first. How did nobody catch that in editing? 
<spoiler>The ending was nice, but I wish we'd seen more of it. I hated Gary (who was Guy in the original books, the girls all learnt the name and should have remembered it, why was this changed?) and they should have broken it off way sooner. Also idk why Nadine and Magda thought it was fine him crashing their lunch, they should have called it out as a major red flag and that should have been what caused the break up.
I wish we saw Ellie learning about her sexuality, coming out to people, etc. -I would have liked that way more than endless Gary/Guy mansplaining dates.
Also the whole Nigel storyline is creepy and went nowhere. Idk how the family thought it was funny, he'd cousin bring a creep and trying to kiss her is not funny at all! 
More Nadine and Magda was needed. What's Magda going through with changing her look and trying to fit in with Chris' friends? We know Ellie doesn't like him but no idea why. 
Nadine has so little story, she's sleeping around apparently and kind of has a thing with her landlord (do we need more creepy men really?), BDSM which would have been great to go into more detail on but no detail is ever given. 
I saw someone say this doesn't feel like women who are fourty based on the language and I agree.
It seems like every straight man is terrible in the story too, it sould be nice to show some decent men. Or even make the book less about men and focus more on the girls! </spoiler>

Title: Somewhere Beyond the Sea
Review:
After having loved the first book, a 5* read which felt like a standalone book, I couldn't not pick up the sequel. 
It's great to be back with the characters we all know and love from the previous story. It's interesting to follow Arthur instead of Linus this time, it's great to get an insight into his head. It also feels like Linus has already had his arc and story, this one is for Arthur (and the kids of course). 
It starts with problems with DICOMY, this time they go to see them and testify in court, which is good setup for the rest of the book, leading to yet another visit from DICOMY to the island, though seeing it from a different point of view is good and Linus asking if they were this nervous for his visit is great. 
The plot about the visit is quite similar to the first book, but with someone a lot less nice than Linus this time, but the core of this story is the kids and how the characters develop for me rather than the plot itself. The introduction of David is good, though again it doesn't change the plot a whole lot but I enjoy seeing what it's like for a new person to arrive and how all the children interract with him. So lovely! 
I'll put more detailed thoughts about where the book goes and the ending below, but overall I did enjoy this book. It's not quite as amazing as the first, but that's a very high bar, this was still a great book. 
<spoiler>This book definitely had more of a an overarching plot than the first with DICOMY, with the court in the beginning to them showing up at the end. Whilst it was good, I think what makes this book is the characters and it's hard to have a full separate DICOMY arc and follow the kids in the 400 pages. It also felt a bit open ended at the end, unlike the first book which felt like a standalone novel, this does feel like it's setting up for a future book, a small pet peeve of mine. 
I'm not sure how I feel about Zoe's story, whilst I love her as a character the Queen bit is a bit odd, adding a monarch into the story just feels slightly weird. I know it's great she's using her power for good, but given how monarchy has been towards marginalised groups in the past it feels a bit weird for me. 
I love how Linus proposed, I loved the wedding at the end and in general I love how the town is becoming more and more accepting of magical beings. It brings me great hope!</spoiler>

Title: Butter
Review:
I've heard a lot about this book and finally got around to reading it. It is a. Little on the slow side but that's on purpose and it does pick up later in the book, I couldn't put it down at the end! 
I listened to the audio and the narration was really good, especially the voice for Manako Kajii was perfect for her - feminine and slightly unhinged. The narrator did pronounce Rika and Reiko with a D sound to my ear, so more like Dika and Deiko, it doesn't take away anything but just thought I'd mention it. Great narration overall though. 
For the actual story I did enjoy it. It's very long for a litfic book, but I read fantasy so I'm used to long books. It's definitely worth it and didn't feel like it was drawn out at all. 
The characters are all really interesting and even though the book started with the plot of did Kajii kill the men, in the end I cared way less about that and more about Rika and the others and how they were doing. 
There is really good commentary on how women's looks are treated in society, eating disorders, body shaming and general sexism especially in the context of Japan. As an English reader it's interesting to hear about sexism in a different culture and the similarities and differences to my own. It's well written and you don't feel preached to, but you learn bits and pieces as you go which I like. 
Reiko's marriage is an interesting topic as well as Rika's relationship. Without spoilers, I like how both are handled throughout the book but even more so their friendship. Female friendships is another theme throughout this book and I like how they are explored. So many books go for romance and it's nice to focus on the women for once. 
I prefer the friendships to the family relationships, family isn't discussed as often  I found but I liked how it was when they did go into it. 
There is a lot of talk about food and cooking, it doesn't go fully in depth on things like how cows are treated but it does touch on them (female cows being forcefully inseminated and such). I wish it did more as opposed to romanticising some of the animal products we eat, but at least it does mention it and doesn't completely gloss over it. 
Overall I enjoyed this book and am glad I read it.

Title: Yesteryear
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. It wasn't what I expected it to be, in a good way. I was expecting a general anti-tradwife book, I didn't expect the nuance and it is darker than I expected. 
Natalie is such a fascinating character and an interesting head to be in. She's definitely an unlikable and somewhat unreliable narrator and it's done really well. You understand where she's coming from and how she's become the person she is, despite knowing she's not a great person. It made me think more about that she is also the victim of the system and that's what we should hate on more than individuals. 
More detailed thoughts in spoilers but overall loved it and would recommend it. 
<spoiler>I really liked the twist, I wasn't expecting it and I'm glad it was that and not some reality show. It's much darker than I was expecting! 
Also I wasn't expecting Caleb to go from a bumbling idiot to being so awful. And Natalie clearly becoming more mentally ill and not recognising anything and being drugged is so sad, I never thought I'd feel sorry for her. 
Only thing I didn't like is her Mum's reveal about her and Natalie's Dad, it didn't add much and felt off. 
I like how it shows that other women aren't ways happy, and it is interesting the overlap with a lot of left leaning women who are becoming anti capitalist, leaning towards community and homesteading and such which is similar in some ways to religion. 
I did love the full circle of at the beginning Natalie said I saw the world and want no part of it to at the end where Clementine says the world is amazing why did you keep it from us. So poetic, no notes. </spoiler>

Title: To Sir, with Love
Review:
I enjoyed this book. I listened to it and the narrator was really good.
The characters are likeable and you root for them throughout the story. It's nice to see the kids change over the year. 
It is definitely an of it's time book, the sexism is a bit jarring sometimes especially as the book highlights the problems with racism, it stands out to me. 
I wouldn't say it's groundbreaking, but it is an interesting story and it's told by a black guy in London in that era which of itself is good as there aren't a lot of books like it. 
I'd recommend it, especially the audiobook.

Title: The Third Form at St. Clare's
The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. I had high expectations and it definitely met them!
Addie is a really interesting character, I like how she's a survivor, she goes through so much and does it well. It can't have been easy and we don't see all of it but she's lived through so much. She's a great main character to follow, she's interesting and unique enough without being annoying and you always want to learn more. 
I found Luc a really different kind of character, you know he's bad from the start and I never grew to like him, though I don't think you're supposed to. The stereotype of men/boys being mean to women/girls they like is a bit grating though. 
I really liked Henry, without spoilers, the sections where he's around are some of my favourites. I just really liked him and was rooting for him like I was Addie. More spoiler thoughts below! 
The ending was great, no spoilers, but I was worried wondering how it would end as I feared it may be some easy way out but it was so well done, I didn't see it coming but it works so well and I felt all the emotions. 
Not quite a five star for me, but definitely a great book and my favourite if the year so far (as of March). 
<spoiler>Spoiler thoughts, I live how Addie and Henry fit so well together because of their wishes, but really that is all it is. They like each other, but really they wouldn't have been together if they'd known each other without that context and I like how it's shown. Plus a relationship could never have worked, all his friends and family constantly forgetting, they could never have kept it up.
I like learning about Henry never being able to believe what's real, it can seem like he's just insecure but never knowing if anyone really likes you can be hard. It's like celebs or rich people, except Henry literally has nobody.
Also a small thing but knowing Luc learned from Addie to be careful with time limits is neat. 
The ending with Addie going off with Luc is a great way to end it, I don't buy Addie liking him really as he's awful and toxic, but using him makes sense and them annoying each other for eternity is a very poetic way to end it, even if it's not a happy ending, it's very fitting and I was so happy there wasn't some magic way to make everyone happy.</spoiler>

Title: Storm Quest
Review:
Another great book in the series. Evil once again is trying to stir up trouble in the Land, Evil is constantly finding new ways it seems.
Claire is an interesting character, especially as she's a bit younger than all the others have at only eighteen. She's unfortunately mature for her age so it doesn't read too young though, which I like. I like the fact for the series that the characters are in their twenties (and somr thirties I'd guess now). 
Good story, a few hints at some bigger issues but not a lot. I like the connection to Jay in too. 
Overall I really enjoyed reading this book. Couldn't put it down!

Title: An Absolutely Remarkable Thing
Review:
It took me a bit to get into this book, but once I was I couldn't put it down! I loved the premise of it. April does annoy me a bit but it gets better as it goes on, not that she's better necessarily but is more self aware. She felt very young at first, almost like I was reading YA, but it got more adult as it went on. I think April is just immature so it read that way. Also I loved Maya and I want to see more of her. Also love Andy as a character too. They're both great.
I'll keeo it spoiler free, I really like having a bi main character. Especially highlighting how people are OK with gay or straight but bi is a problem is underrepresented in media and I really appreciate the representation here. It's minor to the plot but it's important. 
I won't go into too much of the plot, I really like most of it but I'm not sure on the ending. Mostly that it felt like too much of a cliffhanger for a second book. I want to read book two now, but it could have wrapped up more nicely.
Overall a great book and would recommend it.

Title: The House in the Cerulean Sea
Review:
I absolutely loved this book, the best book of the year for me (in April) so far. Definitely one you can binge read, whenever I was reading it I didn't want to put it down.
The main character was a great one to follow and learn about everyone else from his point of view. I really enjoyed exploring via him, how you slowly start to see more and more about everyone and all. A five star read for sure. 
<spoiler>
All the characters inside the house were great in their own ways, they balanced each other out and did feel like a family. I was rooting for them the entire time and hoping nothing would change my mind. Also definitely picked up hints on Arthur and Linjs and so glad it ended the way it did for them. I never expected Linus to move their at the end, I thought he'd be trying to do more from inside DICOMY but I'm glad I was wrong.
His growth throughout the book was really good, I went from not having as many opinions on him and focusing on everyone else to caring about him more and more as the book went on. Love his increased courage at the end, from the villagers to inside DICOMY. </spoiler>

Title: Uncivilised: Ten Lies that Made the West
Review:
A good informative book, filling in a lot of gaps and misconceptions about the history of western civilisation. 
I've knocked off a star as some of the comments I couldn't find sources for, and in one case is wrong, where the author states every prime minister went to the same university (except John Major), when Gordon Brown is another exception - a small thing, but it makes me question other claims in the book.
I did enjoy dreading it and I think I learnt a lot from it and would still recommend it. It's a very accessible book to read for people like me who don't know a lot.

Title: City of Last Chances
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. It took me much longer to read than a lot of fantasy as it's so dense. Initially I did struggle to follow some of the characters and I kept having to refer back to bits, but as I went on I found it easier and could read more in one go.
I like learning about different people and how the Pals are trying to take over the city, depressing as it often is. Without spoilers, generally I liked it, it could have had a bit more of a plot joining some of the characters up, especially in the first half of the book to make it less confusing. 
Overall, would recommend and will continue with the series, though I may need a bit of a break as it is not the easiest of reads. 
<spoiler>Spoiler wise I liked it, I wish we got more of a proper ending and I feel like so much is unknown and unanswered but I guess it is only the first book. There were a few predictable bits like the hanging but most were not, the Hellgram's wife reveal I did not and I loved that. I like how that first game of chaq seemed so causal yet determined so much of the book, was a nice way to show all of those characters together. 
Some of my favourite characters were Lemya, Blackmane and Yasnic. </spoiler>

Title: Stories From The Shetland Witch: In Achaea & Mrs Sinclair and the Feather Haa
Review:
Two fun short stories that sit alongside the original book.
Both interesting but I found the second story much more so than the first one.
Just a personal preference, I enjoyed the characters more and learning more about the history of witches in the Shetlands. The first one was a bit too much of the annoying Greek gods, I prefer the witches in the original story and I do here. 
Hard to rate as its quite short so I gave it a four the same as the original, as it's of equal quality and is interesting back story.

Title: On the Greenwich Line
Review:
This was a really interesting book to read. It's a perspective I've not read about before and I enjoyed learning about all the different people and the lives they lead.
For a short book I learnt a lot and would definitely recommend it. 
<spoiler>I wish there was either more of a plot or less of a plot. Which sounds odd, but I would have rather ended with an actual funeral or information about what happened. Otherwise I think it would have been better to spend less time on the funeral plot and more exploring the characters in other ways. It felt like it was trying to include a plot but not fully, which made it feel half done in a sense. 
Still a really good book though. </spoiler>

Title: Girls Out Late
Review:
A good sequel to the girls series.
Short and fun, it ages well as teens are always lying to their parents about bring out late. Friends vs relationships is also a timeless debate. 
Still a teen focused book but a nice nostalgia read as an adult.

Title: Murder at the Black Cat Cafe
Review:
A fun mystery book, if you want a shortish read with an interesting well thought out plot I'd recommend it.
It's quite short, the additional short story is almost as long as the book, but it's not bad to read a short short sometimes. 
I also appreciate that it meant the story wasn't dragged out in any way, the twists and turns weren't obvious and it went through at a good pace so you could be surprised by it.
One of the quotes on the back was that it's "A Japanese Agatha Christie" and whilst there are some differences in the way the story is told and how the detective is, I'd say it's a fairly apt descriptor and if you like Agatha Christie you'll probably enjoy this too. 
Overall a good read.

Title: Tales from the Café
Review:
A good story, but a bit more similar to the first than I'd like.
Some interesting stories, but it's starting to get a bit same-y and not sure if I'm going to carry on with the series as I'm not sure how many different tales of people going back can be that different anymore. Meeting a dead friend or relative, a past lover, it is starting to blur about it. 
It's good if you want a nice quick easy read, but it's less exciting than the first, where you're learning about this interesting coffee shop.

Title: I'm Glad My Mom Died
Review:
It's hard to review this incredible book. It is such a sad story and the way it is written is so well done.
I would highly recommend the audiobook for this, Jennette narrates it herself and hearing her voice herself as a child is chilling when saying things that seem so normal to her that are so very far from it. 
The book doesn't shy away from a lot of difficult topics, child actors in Hollywood, obviously how her Mom treats her, so I'd definitely recommend reading trigger warnings if anything is relevant. 
She tells her story so well, you feel like you know this child and want to do something but all you can do is listen to everything happening and take it in it is far from an easy read but it is one I would recommend to so many people as it is such a good book. 
No notes, an incredible book, easy five star for me.
Content Warnings: Graphic: Body shaming, Cancer, Child abuse, Death, Eating disorder, Emotional abuse, Terminal illness, Death of parent; Moderate: Addiction, Adult/minor relationship, Alcoholism, Domestic abuse, Panic attacks/disorders, Vomit, Alcohol, Sexual harassment;

Title: The Remarkable Retirement of Edna Fisher
The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time
How to Stop Time
Review:
I really enjoyed reading this book. It was one of those where I couldn't put it down and had to know what was going to happen, but not too much so where you almost start skimming as you're desperate to know what's next. 
It's a great concept and it was executed pretty well overall. The characters were all interesting and I always wanted to learn more about them. 
A couple of minor nitpicks in spoilers below. Overall great book though! 
<spoiler>I wish we learnt a bit more about the world overall with the Albas, we learnt some but I could have used more. Especially as a lot of what we were told is probably lies, it is never clear. We're people really being disappeared, was the Berlin thing real? 
The ending felt like a bit rushed to, it could have had some more explanation and learning about what the world is really like would have been great. Maybe a chapter going to some scientific place or something would have helped. 
It's not a massive complaint, I just felt a bit left hanging at the end and I need more! 
</spoiler>

Title: Cloud Atlas
Review:
It's a really interesting book to read, very well written. It took me a bit to get into it as the initial perspective wasn't my favourite, but every time it changed I ended up liking it more and more. At first I read a few chapters a day, but the second half of the book I couldn't out down. 
I loved this book and it will definitely stick with me. 
<spoiler>
I definitely preferred some bits to others, the initial character didn't resonate as much but I absolutely loved the middle story with the fabricant and the mystery of Luisa Rey.
It was really interesting hearing all the differenct perspectives on life in different times and places, I wish some of them overlapped a bit more though. The fabricant section was my favourite but I was hoping for more overlap with it.
I read this book over a couple of weeks and I would forget earlier references later on, I felt like I needed a guide on which stories connect where. Also I know there is meant to be reincarnation of souls between them, but I didn't follow that exactly as some of the stories have overlap and it wasn't clear who was necessarily who. It didn't stop my enjoyment of it though. 
It makes rating it hard as some bits I would say are five star, but the others didn't capture me in the same way and it was a bit hard to get into so I've put 4.5 as an average for the book.
 </spoiler>

Title: I Bet You'd Look Good in a Coffin
The Christmas Cottage
Review:
I liked this book much more than I thought I would. I had low expectations as I'm not always a fan of romance and was worried it would be too much like a hallmark movie but it pleasantly surprised me. It still has some of the usual tropes, overworked city woman ends up in the countryside for Christmas, but some of the way things happened surprised me and I enjoyed that. Also the romance wasn't the main focus of the book, rather the other relationships between the different POV characters and they were all way more interesting.
More thoughts in spoilers, but overall a nice cosy book to read at Christmas. Nothing groundbreaking, but a good read. 
<spoiler>I liked the fact that the little romance had no drama really and was just there - it was pretty obvious so I'm glad it wasn't a major plot point. I also enjoyed the surprise of them being related, didn't see that coming and exploring those dynamics was interesting. It was interesting nothing with Tina was ever resolved, usually everything is wrapped up neatly in these kind of books but this is more realistic and I appreciate that. </spoiler>

Title: Katabasis
Review:
A really great book!
It was interesting to read, I like stories based in universies and schools as well as fantasy so this is great for me. I also like fantasy following adults and not teens which is needed more. 
I like the premise, the paradoxes are fun but you can also skim over them and just enjoy the vibes of them without understanding them, which is a nice balance of being academic but not overwhelmingly so. 
Hell is really well done, how it compares to other hells is a nice touch too. How all the areas are described is really well done. 
Alice is an odd character, not very relatable but a great person to follow. Peter is a good counterpart to have alongside her, I like the back and forth between them and how they work together. 
Professor Grimes, not a fan, more thoughts in spoilers. Good character but bad person! 
Overall a good book, would recommend it to people who like a fantasy dark academia, but it's more niche than a lot of other fantasy. 
<spoiler>The more I read the more I started to dislike all the characters. Alice is so morally grey but it makes her a more interesting head to be inside. Professor Grimes is awful, unfortunately unsurprisingly given men of the era in academia, but still. Yikes. The ending was good, twisty but not in an annoying way or so obvious. So glad we got Peter over Grimes! Peter's death always felt temporary to me though, off scene ones always do, so I don't think I was as shocked as u could have been. 
Liked it overall though. </spoiler>

Title: The City  of Brass
Review:
I really enjoyed this book overall.
It starts of at a slower pace but does ramp up, especially at the end, so I put it at medium but it's more like 3/4 slow and 1/4 fast. 
The world is really interesting, sometimes I got a bit confused as there is so much world building, but not so much that I couldn't understand what was going on. More just at the end of the book I looked up a few things to clarify them. 
It's a very politics heavy book with all the different tribes, the history and between them and the current ongoing of the city.
My minor complaint is that is definitely feels like the first book in a series. I was reading the second half of the book, desparate to get to a good conclusion, and was disappointed that most things don't get resolved. A lot of this book does feel like setup for future books. My hope is that it pays off and I'll enjoy the other books more so because of it, but it annoys me when the first book feels like it isn't a complete book in itself which this book kind of feels like.
Overall I did enjoy it and will continue to read this series.
Content Warnings: Graphic: Death, Slavery, Religious bigotry, Colonisation, War, Classism; Minor: Death of parent, Fire/Fire injury, Deportation;

Title: Blue Sisters
Moods: dark, emotional, hopeful, inspiring, reflective, sad
Review:
I really enjoyed reading this book.
It is very character based and follows the three sisters as they navigate life after the death of their fourth sister. They all are struggling in different ways and it's an interesting insight into the many different ways of dealing with grief and it mixing with the many other issues in people's lives. If you love a book about flawed characters then this is a great choice. 

<spoiler>It was great to see the flawed characters and they all did grow, though in some cases they had to spiral down first. I wouldn't say any of the characters are super likeable, perhaps Bonnie is, but Avery cheating and Lucky doing everything made them really unlikeable to me. It's OK as I don't think every character has to be, but it may not be for everyone. I do think them learning and becoming better people was well done and sometimes you need need to start with a not so great character to have that journey so I didn't mind it too much. Sometimes I wished there was just someone a bit less flawed, if only for reference, which Chiti kind of was but she wasn't frequent enough to make an impact with it. 
It would have been good to explore the relationship with the mother a bit more, it felt a little tacked on and didn't seem like it added much to the story. Which is fine as it's about the sisters but I didn't get why it was included. </spoiler>

Overall a great book, I couldn't put it down and had to finish it in an evening.

Title: Water Moon
Review:
This was a really well written and interesting book I thoroughly enjoyed reading. The whole premise I'd describe as in some ways a more ethereal fantasy within our world, but with some much darker undertones which were explored throughout the book. 
I thought Hana and Keishin are a good combination of characters to follow. Their differences but also similarities in how stubborn they are make for a great pair, interesting dialog and the choices they make always make sense, I'm never frustrated as I always get why they do what they do.
The world building is so fun, I love it, you have to accept a lot just on how it is but so does Kei and it just works. You just keep thinking of course that is a thing, why wouldn't it be! 
Without spoilers, a really great story, the symbolism is strong and it plays out in a really interesting way I did not see coming. Their are twists that are good but not too out there to be unrealistic. 
I did knock down my rating a bit, mostly due to some bits of the ending, more details in spoilers. Overall I loved the book, would recommend it. 
<spoiler>I really enjoyed the part how they are chasing their parents, Hana literally but also Kei in a sense and how their stories are tied together more than you realise. 
I love the world, from travelling by puddles and rumours to a village that creates the night sky. 
Also how everything is set in stone and no choices can be made is not a unique concept but it's done well here. The Shiikiun are a great concept that shows the world is not as nice as it seems and it unravels more and more as you learn alongside Kei which is well done. You get shocked when he does! 
There are lots of twists and turns with Hana, I like most of them, it keeps you on your toes and really makes you think and second guess things. 
My only thing I didn't like was the ending. I like how the parents are handled, but her and Kei just finding each other seemed too neat and was very quickly done, I feel like there could have been more there. 
Otherwise, great book! </spoiler>

Title: Life of Pi
