Review: I'm definitely glad I read this book. It's not like anything else I've read, mostly in a good way. There is a little too much of the actual journey (too many gory details for my liking!) but none the less is a great story. A boy and a lion. You would never expect anything like what happens, but it does. It's not necessarily relate-able, but you just want to read more and more of this book.

Title: Demon Lupus
Review:
Overall a good story, I liked it but not as much as the first book.
This book has a few ties to the first book but is mostly a separate story. It is focused on werewolves/shapeshifters which I personally find less interesting than witches, but if you are a big werewolf fan this is the one of the series you'll love the most. 
I like the more politics side of things, truces, traitors, all that stuff interests me more. 
The story overall is decent but I didn't find myself connecting with Lily like I did Amethyst as much which is why I don't think I loved the story like I did last time. Maybe she's a bit too much of a moody teen for me. 
Also not a spoiler but there are a few more sexual bits, nothing outrageous but some of it read weird to me, not in it being explicit but the way some of the men thought. 
I kept having mixed feelings towards the rest of the group, sometimes I liked them sometimes I hated them, definitely morally greyish which is interesting. 
I did enjoy the book though, but I'm much more looking forward to the next one. It's a good book, just hard to review it and not compare how amazing the first book was in my eyes.

Title: Dust Settles North
Review:
I was given an advanced e-reader copy via NetGalley in exchange for a review. 

This is a really good book and different to a lot of what is out there. Which is a shame, I wish more books like this could get published. 
Following Hannah and Zain is an interesting way of seeing how different people greive, particularly as they're both at a point in their life where they don't really know what they want. The book shows how grief really well and I appreciate that. 
It's definitely a slower paced book and more character driven than plot. There is some talk about the politics in Egypt at the time, but I would really call that plot exactly. I'd recommend this to people who prefer character focused books and not to people prefer more plot driven books. 
I like the being caught between two cultures, when you're raised in one but visit another. It's a complex situation, navigating feeling like you're not part of either world and again I've not seen this enough in literature and it really should be more prevelent, especially in this day and age.
I definitely can relate to this, though the two cultures for me are less different then USA and Egypt, but this book has made me want to book a trip back ASAP. I love it when a story makes an impact like that. 
The book is well written, it's slice of life and jumps back and forth between times a bit which can be confusing, you have to double check the years sometimes but I generally liked the format. No chapters in my copy, just a year with sometimes a season and who is talking. It did work well though, but I would have liked more flashbacks of her mother, the ones we got were great and I needed more about her activism and growing up in Egypt and about Nora and Hamada too.
Overall, really enjoyed this book. It'd easy to read, you can binge it in one or read it a bit day by day and it still works.

Title: Pride: The Unlikely Story of the True Heroes of the Miner's Strike
The Museum of Ordinary People
Review:
I absolutely loved reading this book. It's the first book by Mike Gayle I've read and I'm itching to read more now.
There were a few things I wasn't 100% on which docks it down from a 5*, but I have very few complaints with this book. 

<spoiler>
I loved the journey Jess went on throughout this book. From being lost in all parts of her life to finding something that brings her joy, the museum. 
The characters were great, aside from Guy who you are clearly meant to hate. He seemed a little one dimensional and their relationship was a little predictable, but as it's not the focus of the story it's a minor complaint. I wish she'd realised herself how awful he was treating her rather than him breaking things off though.
I loved the museum and everyone they worked there. Alex and his story was great, how people treated him and his back story was done very well. I didn't see it coming, I was predicting in my head and I didn't figure out out, which I enjoyed. 
I'm still not sure how I feel about her father twist at the end, I think the issue was it was so close to the end that it didn't seem to matter. A small fallout that instantly was fixed, it seemed a bit pointless. </spoiler>

Title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
Review: Started listening to this, some bits are interesting but some of the phrasing and such seemed a bit off. This led me to look up reviews and it appears this book is not as factual as I was hoping. It's not completely false information, more like picking and choosing which theories to present to have a narrative. That plus other criticisms have made me decide to drop it.

Title: Seer Quest
Review:
Loved this book, also one of my favourite ones in the whole series.
I've been wanting to see a Seer ever since the first book and finally got my wish. Also means I got to learn much more about the wider grid, as Seers need to know such things of course.
Liz's journey is really interesting and without giving away too much it doesn't necessarily follow a similar structure to the rest of the quests, she knows much more of what she's getting into than most of the others did. 
Great book, enjoying my reread and leaving full reviews for them all now as I love this series.

Title: Such a Fun Age
Review:
I enjoyed reading this, it was an easy read and was keen to finish it and couldn't put it down.
The way racism was handled was interesting, but it would have been nicer to have a bit more from Emira or other black characters instead of all about how white people see racism. 
Overall a good read though, 3.5.

<spoiler>
The ending was odd but I didn't mind it, I like when I don't see things coming. I wish it was done a bit better though, it seemed a bit too much of a 180 in the character. I know it's meant to show she's an unreliable narrator, but there could have been more done to show that side of her character earlier on so it felt less out of left field, in my opinion. 
It would have been nicer to see Emira grow a bit more as a person and hear about her instead of Alix and Kelley so much. </spoiler>

Title: Return to the DallerGut Dream Department Store
Review:
Great book, I enjoyed it just as much as the first book which is always hard for a sequel. 
This book expands on the universe, also getting a bit more info on the real world which is interesting. 
Whilst we are following Penny, most of the story and character development is about everyone else around her. It's more lots of little stories in some ways. More info in spoilers.
Overall so glad I got to return to the Dallergut Dream Department Store and I hope I get to go back one day. 
<spoiler>I really liked the disability focus, how you dream whilst blind, but I wish it was a bit longer. 
There are lots of small things, like fortune cookies, the caves, chasing non returning customers. 
The pyjamas party was fun but not sure it added a lot, but I did like how it brought the theme of memories, which is in some way the theme of the book. </spoiler>

Title: Minor Larceny
Review:
This was a really interesting read, not exactly what I was expecting but that's not a bad thing.
It's nice to read a book where the main characters are all 70+, unusual and I appreciate it. Definitely a bit of boomer humour to go with it, but it fits the characters.
Without any spoiler, the story did not end up where I expected but I enjoyed it none the less. More thoughts in spoilers, but overall it was well done, a good read and glad I impulse bought this. 
I also appreciate the way sexism was handled, John clearly is a bit sexist and the woman all call it out appropriately - eg. him buying the pink notebook for the women, then they make him use it. It's realistic and I like that he clearly does learn from small things like that throughout the story. It rings true for a man brought up in that era, and I like that he doesn't brush it off and listens to Sal and Jules. Not just for that but also for things like doing too much himself without consulting the team, then he admits he was wrong and says he'll do better. Love to see it! 
<spoiler>Story was good, the care being so different to what they initially started out to do which I didn't expect but it worked out well. I was hoping we'd see multiple cases, but this one was in depth. 
I know it's a we may never know thing, but it would be nice to get closure on the are Jules and John related thing, it was hinted at a few times but nothing ever came of it. </spoiler>

Title: Abroad in Japan
Review: Interesting book on Japan, read it before I went and was glad I did.

Title: The Body in the Library
Review:
An interesting mystery. I found it better than the first one as there was much more Miss Marple and the narrator was clearer.
My only criticism is that I wish she didn't keep saying I know who did it but not telling anyone for no apparent reason. At least an excuse about no evidence or something would have sufficed. It happened multiple times too which felt unnecessary. 
Generally I really enjoyed the book and want to read more Miss Marple.

Title: Guardian Quest
Review:
I was a bit surprised to get this book as I thought the previous one would be the last, but I'm not complaining about another quest!
It's nice to see a Worlder come in, have an interesting ability and solve an issue, this feels more akin to some of the earlier books which we haven't had a while so I'll take it. I like the main character, interesting backstory and works well with the issue, trying it be vague enough so not to spoil it but I very much enjoyed the plot and character development. Only thing that slight annoyed me is the romance was a bit much and more explicit than previous books. Not ridiculously so but more than necessary, I find myself skimming some of those bits. 
Without giving away too much, this book does feel a bit like an epilogue in the way it does try and tie up some of the loose ends with Jay and Claire from the last book, though more so Claire, I wish we had another where we saw more of Jay.

Title: The Shadow of What Was Lost
Review:
I could not put this book down, despite it's length I read it over three days as I just wanted to know what was going to happen.
It's definitely more plot driven than characters, not to say you're not invested in them, but it's more focused on the plot. 
The world building is great too, though occasionally I may have to go back and check something as there are a lot of people and places introduced on the side which can be a lot. 
It is a good book in itself, but it is definitely the setup for a trilogy. 
Also I hope it gets better but some of the woman could be written a bit better, one jarring scene especially - <spoiler>Davian suddenly seems obsessed with how pretty someone is, it's so out of place and definitely is a men writing women vibe which I wasn't a fan of. </spoiler> Asha is great though :). Needed more of her development for sure. 
Knocked off a small amount for the slight confusions and wishing it felt a bit like it's too much setup for later books. I did love this book and would highly recommend to anyone who likes plot based high fantasy with great world building.

Title: Fantastic Beasts & Where to Find Them
Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
Under the Whispering Door
Review:
I absolutely loved this book!
I've been slowly reading through all of TJ Klune's books after loving A House in the Cerulean Sea and this one didn't disappoint. 
Wallace and Hugo are great, though they really reminded me of Linus and Arthur from Cerulean Sea - <spoiler> maybe a bit too similar as it basically made me predict the entire arc of their story - 
</spoiler> but I did like the dynamic between them, plus the rest of the family. Mei is great at her job and I love her and Nelson is hilarious. 
It's a great feel good story which is exactly what I wanted going into it, despite it heavily featuring death. 
More thoughts on plot in spoilers below, but overall a good book and I loved reading it and couldn't put it down. 
Wallace has a great story, his character growth and arc is lovely and I want more books with arcs like this. 
<spoiler>The ending is a bit of a twist, very out of nowhere. I wasn't too surprised as I figured something bizarre would happen to get Wallace to stay, but it did feel very deus ex machina. I didn't care too much as I was really wanting him to stay but I can see some people not liking it. </spoiler>

Title: Unseen: How I Lost My Vision But Found My Voice
Review:
I loved this book!
I've watched Molly for a while on YouTube and was so excited when this came out I bought it on release but I waited to listen to it instead and I'm so glad I did. She's a great narrator and as it's a book by a blind author about her life it seems an appropriate way to consume it. Also not a really a spoiler but in the audiobook she references an event and uses the clip from herself talking at the event which was really cool. 
I really enjoyed this book, we need more disability representation and this helps with that. Molly is a great advocate and the world is lucky to have her. As an able bodied person I'm trying to educate myself more and this book is really good for that. 
It is well written, you feel her emotions as you're listening to her describe life events, it's like you're on the rollercoaster of her life with her. 
Some stories could have gone into more depth, but some of that could be to legal reasons. Also more life events maybe could have been included. I just wanted more! It did feel on the shorter side. 
My only other criticism, which I find in her videos too sometimes, is that whilst I love how positive she is I find she overdoes it on how visualising a better future will make it happen and how she just refuses to be a victim. I get it works for her, but so many people have the same wishes and just being positive and visualising a better future isn't going to work for a lot of people, especially unfortunately disabled people in our society. It's great to hear her success but I'm not a fan of the just believe in yourself message as unfortunately that isn't how it works for a lot of people in reality.
I get it is great for her and it is her memoir, but wanted to mention it as I know it could be frustrating for some people. 
Still loved the book though!

Title: Book Lovers
Review:
I'm not normally a romance reader but I really enjoyed this book.
The characters were interesting and I enjoyed following them on there different journeys. I liked it much more than I thought I was going to. 
<spoiler>
As someone who dislikes city women finding their true love in some small town, I like the twist on that take here. Sure they all discovered themselves in some way, but I like a story where a woman gets to continue having her career, remains childfree and is happy about all of it. It seems far too rare. I liked the sisters being close and in the end them accepting they won't live nearby anymore but that it's the best decision for them felt like real growth, plus hits home far too much as it's often the case in reality. You won't be able to be by your friends/family's sides forever and it's sad but that's life and I really liked how it was handled here. </spoiler>

Title: The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet
Last Night at the Telegraph Club
A Story for Every Day of Winter
Review:
It's a collection of short stories so hard to answer a lot of questions about it.
I enjoyed reading them, they was a good variety in genre too. Most of them were good, a few were amazing. The lengths varied, I could have done with some being shorter to be more consistent.
If you're in a reading rut and need something to read each day I'd highly recommend this.

Title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
The Diary of a Bookseller
Review:
It was interesting to start with but it was a bit repetitive by the end. There's only many different things that happen which makes sense, but it may have been better to condense or skip those days.
Also I get the slightly rude attitude towards customers, but I was really put off by the way the author talked about libraries and library books. Most people into books really appreciate libraries and it was so jarring reading those comments about them. 
I did enjoy this book at the star, but it felt a bit like a chore to finish. There was nothing particularly gripping but I suppose that's what it's supposed to be. It's a regular person's diary for a year, which for most people isn't that interesting aside from a few key things. 
I heard he's releasing another book and I'm not sure if I'll bother with it.

Title: All the Lonely People
Review:
I loved this book, it's been a while since I was so attached to characters. The unlikely friendships that form and I was just rooting for Hubert the entire time. 
Amazing book, no notes. Would definitely recommend. 
<spoiler>I like that while there are some big twists, it's not like you're expecting them. What do you mean Rose never existed? My worries about him lying to her the entire time were for nothing, I was so shocked at that. Unfortunately I was less surprised that David never returned. Hubert really had no family left, but it was great he did find the friends. I just wish he'd was around to enjoy it more.
</spoiler>

Title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
The Familiar
Review:
It took a while for me to get into the book, but once I did I really started to enjoy it and wanted to carry on reading it. Towards the end especially I didn't want to put it down. 
It is a well written story, I really liked Luiza as a complex character and having a few chapters from other perspectives really added to the story. 
Without saying too much, Santángel and Valentina are my other favourite characters and I found their separate stories added to the main story as well and getting bits of them throughout, not all at once but just enough to keep you wanting more. 
More thoughts in spoilers on the plot. 
Also it isn't ever talked about how magic works or the world, but the way the story is told it doesn't really matter as that's not what is important here. 
Feeling all kinds of thoughts and emotions, the sign of a good book! 
<spoiler>
I was surprised at how much of the story was taken up by the torneo, I it seemed to go on for ages but it makes sense in the end why it does. 
I found it interesting Gracia thought everyone was a fraud, it shows a bit of the world and how everyone else sees the ones who do have powers of a sort. 
Haulit's story is a mixed bag, I was annoyed at her sometimes and so sad for her at others. A tragic ending as she had so much hope, but it makes sense how it all happened. 
Santángel was such an interesting character, I kept speculating about him and was really happy with the ending and how he grew and his arc went. I wasn't sure about the romance at first, but given where it lead I was happy in the end. 
Also surprisingly I started liking Valentina more and more over the course of the story and learning about her was great. So glad she managed to leave her awful husband and be with the playwright at the end, being a motherly figure to the girls who needed it. I didn't think much of her at the start, grew to love her by the end. 
I was happy with the ending, whilst them surviving whilst everyone thinks they're dead is a bit of a trope I think it works well here and I was happy for the two of them. </spoiler>

Title: Carry On
Review:
It was a good book, just not my top favourite.
I loved fangirl so was excited to pick this up, but I didn't live it as much. It was still good and I'll probably read the rest of the series but I'm not hurrying out to read it ASAP.

Title: The Moving Finger
Review:
A fun mystery novel. I'm reading through all the Miss Marple books right now, this is good but not my favourite. 
Not much Miss Marple in it, I wish she was brought in earlier on, this is one of the reasons I didn't like this as much. 
The book is from the point if view if Jerry, who often I find annoying but isn't too bad for a main character. Him and his sister are new to the village so are a good audience insert. 
The plot was interesting, I kept suspecting different people throughout the book and kept changing my mind which is good. 
Of course only Miss Marple knows the answer and figures it all out at the end. 
<spoiler>I found the relationship with Megan kind of creepy, which is what brought it down. It felt odd, out of nowhere and there is a massive age gap. Plus he keeps asking and not taking no until she caves. Not a great look. </spoiler>

Title: Spectacles
Review:
I really enjoyed this book and learning more about her life.
It is what you'd expect, she has some interesting stories, nothing groundbreaking, but it's all told in a humerous way and it's easy to sit back and read/listen to. 
I listened to this as she narrates it herself and does it really well, I'd recommend it.

Title: Wizard Quest
Review:
Another great entry in the series. Also it's nice to have some continuity, as this book does pick up a lot more from past books, it's definitely not as standalone as some of the earlier quests. More world building, it's making the series more interesting and complex which I like.
I'm also liking learning more about wizards, we've not really learnt much since the first book and this one goes into much more detail which I appreciate. 
More hints of evil and tiny bits of info about the grid are good too. I always like more info.

Title: The Murder at the Vicarage
Review:
An interesting story, wish we had more of Miss Marple though. Would have rather followed her more than the vicar.
A fun easy book, will probably continue with the series but I'm not in a rush to do so.

Title: Seven Kinds of People You Find in Bookshops
Review:
Better than The Diary of a Bookseller, I think keeping it short is better.
It's a fun short book, the humour is very specific and may not be everyone's thing but I did enjoy it most of the time.
It's definitely a dangerous game writing a book to appeal to readers which makes fun of stereotypical readers of different kinds. 
Nothing groundbreaking but it's a good read. Especially good if you want a small book to take with you in your bag, it's easy to pick up if you're waiting 10 minutes here and there.

Title: A Promised Land
Review:
It's a really interesting story, I didn't know much about before he became president which was good to learn.
As a non US citizen I found this an accessible way to learn about US politics without it being overwhelming or too complicated. 
This book does what you'd expect, it covers his story, including some of his younger years and before he was president but focusing on how he got elected and through to Osama Bin Laden. I believe there is going to be a second book to follow on.
I listened to this via audio book and he reads it himself, which I would highly recommend.

Title: The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants
Oracle Quest
Review:
The first in the quest series and what made me want to read them all.
The start of everything, I love following Katie and learning all about the Land alongside her. It makes you want to be able to take a trip there too! 
Love the world, the story and everything. It can be easily a standalone story but it also opens the door for all the future books. 
Would definitely recommend!

Title: The Moon is a Door
Review:
I was given an eARC for free on NetGalley in exchange for a review. 

I really enjoyed this book. I was hoping for a fun, easy read about a witchy school and it definitely fit the bill. I read through it in a day as I couldn't put it down! 
I liked Astrid as a protagonist, though I would say she reads as younger than she is, if it wasn't specified she was seventeen I would have guessed maybe fifteen. Even though she was home schooled for magic, she went to a regular school so it seemed odd (also I found it odd they said high school as in the UK we mostly use secondary school). 
I like how the magic system works, that even though Astrid is powerful it's not only due to blood as her mother didn't come from a powerful bloodline. Her communicating with nature and books is interesting and I hope we see more of that going forward. 
The other schoolkids were good, I found it a little predictable but considering it's young adult that's to be expected. We didn't get the ages of them, but again I read some of them as younger. I really liked Cordelia as a character, she was one of my favourites and I kept wanting to know more about her. 
A really small thing but I like that a lot of people have regular names, even the big name families. 
Also, I like that romance isn't a big thing too. So many fantasy or YA books shoehorn in romance, while it's lightly touched on (with teenagers it's hard not to) it's done well here. 
More thoughts in spoilers below, but overall I enjoyed it. I don't read as much YA as I used to, but I grew up obsessed with Harry Potter and do love a good witchy story. Have to wait ages until the next one now, annoying as I do feel there's a lot left hanging and I need answers! 

<spoiler>The three girls, Selene, Lilith and Rosemary definitely had off vibes from the start. Like it was obvious they were going to be bad news, though I did not think it would go as far as it did! It makes you think you know what will happen, which is right, so you don't think further and you're still surprised which I like. Though I do wonder how a seventeen year old orchestrated a powerful witches death, no details are given. It seems a bit unbelievable, I hope we find out more but not sure how we will. 
I hope Selene is off for good, but seeing Lilith and maybe Rosemary a little more in the future would be interesting. Not as friends, but I just want to know how they turn out as people. 
We needed more Cordelia, her French history, what Selene was hinting at, so much is unresolved! I need to know it. 
Also the possessing thing? It didn't seem like Selene as she didn't want Astrid dead, guess that's another mystery for future books. </spoiler>

Title: In the Lives of Puppets
Moods: adventurous, emotional, inspiring, mysterious, reflective, sad
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. I wasn't sure what to expect going in but I started to love the characters as I got to know them and I was rooting for them the whole time. 
<spoiler>This was so emotional, especially when Giovanni destroyed his own heart I loved it but was almost in tears. The whole story was great, from the general plot to each character. Rambo is my favourite for sure though. 
The romance between Hap and Vic felt a bit sudden and out of nowhere, I liked it but there could have been a better build up for it. 
Also there were a couple of bits that I wanted to rush through (descriptive fight scenes felt a bit much, could have been a bit shorter). 
Overall loved this book.</spoiler>

Title: The Book of Beginnings
Review:
I enjoyed this book. I liked following all the different characters and it's great to learn about all their different perspectives.
I didn't want to put it down, it's nice and easy to read and a good book to binge. It's nice and uplifting but not in a cheesy way. I appreciate the focus on friendships over relationships for a lot of the book. 
<spoiler>I liked Jo's relationships with Ruth and Malcolm, definitely the strongest part of the book. Would have taken some more ghost chapters too! 
Would have liked to see more Lando and Eric, I thought we'd be seeing much more of them from the start, but I prefer Ruth and Malcolm I think so it's not too much of a loss.
Her friendship with Lucy is a bit odd, for best friends they don't seem to care about each other sometimes, at least Lucy about Jo. I know people grow apart, but it just seems a bit weird, no texts about missing you, the hiding cheating thing. Maybe we just needed more of it, or an insight into Lucy, but it definitely feels like something was missing. 
Also as a personal thing, I'm not a massive fan of pregnancy in general, but it really didn't seem to add much to the story here. Apart from her wanting a kid, which seems a bit irrelevant for most of the story, plus Lucy also being pregnant didn't add a lot. Maybe it's just me, but if none of it was in there I don't think it would change the story. 
I love the stationery store, wish we had more of those in real life. Even if it's kind of unrealistic nowadays, I like to think her new store did well up north. </spoiler>

Title: Healer Quest
Review:
The long awaited Healer is here! Since it was first mentioned I've been so curious about it and wanted to see one, so glad we finally got Jessi here. 
Interesting plot, seeing how she handles the disease in the Land and how it affects everyone is well done. Also tying into the Land politics as well as with Evil and their plans is done nicely, it all goes together, maybe well is the wrong word but story wise it all lines up even if not in a good way. 
Feels like more and more is building up with Evil, looking forward to the next book as they're definitely not backing down now!

Title: You've Been Pooping All Wrong
Review:
An interesting book to read. Short and to the point which is how I like my non fiction. 
I listened to this, narrator is Patricia Rodriguez. Mostly good but has the issue with some s's getting drawn out in hissing sounds (I think an editing issue), if you're the kind of person who hears high pitched noises this may bother you. It did for me and I just powered through, for a longer book or a book I was less interested in I may have dropped it. 
Generally good info about gut health, some I already knew and some I didn't. Some useful things I knew already about fibre and bidets, a lot of the science and history I didn't know though. Definitely targeted towards the average person who knows little about this, I wish more detail was given in some places but I understand that it's intentionally more vague on some of the science and focused on more realistic steps people can do to improve their health. 
Not sure about the food bit though, whilst some dyes and such are bad, in general ultra processed foods aren't an issue in their own right. Some ultra processed foods are very healthy and lots of ingredients doesn't equal unhealthy in the same way a bag of pure sugar isn't as healthy. 
Overall a decent book, solid 3.5 rating.

Title: Intermezzo
Review:
This was an interesting book to read. The first chapter was really hard to get through, but it got easier and you get used to the writing style a bit more. Peter's chapters are always a bit more difficult to read I found though. 
Initially I found myself preferring Ivan's chapters, though by the end I did like both. I do also like that we got to hear from Margaret and Sylvia, but I wish we got Naomi too. 
This book does a good job of showing how grief affects people and how complicated family relationships are affected by it, in a more day to day way. 
I found the characters interesting, Margaret is my favourite and I'm glad we got to learn more about her family and backstory with her ex. 
Sylvia is a bit more odd, more thoughts in spoilers, but I think we didn't get enough of her. Same with Naomi, why none if her POV? 
I love the dog, always good to add in. Christine is weird about it and I hate her for everything she doesn't do. 
Overall an alright book, I enjoyed bits more than others. I also feel it didn't need to be as long as it is, it could have used some edits. It's well written but sometimes it gets a bit much and it's easy to get lost in what you're reading as it doesn't always make complete sense. 
<spoiler>Lots of depression and suicidal mentions especially towards the end, not too surprising but it's done well I think, the writing style does help with putting you in their head in cases like this and I thought it was well done. 
I like learning about Margaret and her ex, but it makes no sense that not even her friend had her back with him, given everything else we learn about Anna it doesn't add up to me. For Sylvia, I wish we learnt more about her history and the past relationship. Given we get no details on the accident, an odd choice in itself, it's hard to understand why they broke up and even in her POV I didn't fully get it. It seemed intentionally vague but it just left me more confused. Also no mention of her family at all is a bit odd. 
I like Naomi, but I wish we got more of her. It's not clear what she's OK with, monogamy or not, in my head I imagine she's seeing other people too but it isn't clear.
The ending is a choice for Peter/Naomi/Sylvia. I get polyamory is a valid life choice, but starting out a relationship by cheating doesn't seem the best way to go about it. Plus with it still not being clear exactly what's going on with Sylvia I don't know what to think.
I love Ivan and Margaret and Alexei and hope they are happy together forever. </spoiler>

Title: The Hobbit, or There and Back Again
Turtles All the Way Down
Review:
It was a good book, not my favourite of John Green's but a solid book.
The characters are interesting, the main character is very well written and I enjoyed reading about her and everyone surrounding her.

Title: The Will of the Many
Review:
I loved this book. Glad I read the Licanius trilogy first, but this book is definitely better for me.
The story overall is good, Vis is an interesting character to follow and I find the whole world fascinating (in a terrible way!) and want to keep learning more about it. 
Callidus is one of my favourite characters and I also really like Eidhin, more in spoilers below. 
Also I want to see more of Lanistia too, I want more of her background. 
Without any spoilers, I really liked the ending, though in a way it brings more questions than answers. I need to read the next book now! 
<spoiler>I loved Callidus, why did he have to die, he seems like the only real friend for so much of the story. Maybe he'll appear somehow in the other universes? So sad, I can't believe it. Just on the page, suddenly. He warned Vis people died, then it was him. 
I liked Eidhin's arc too, it was really well done and happy that Vis and him are friends now at least.
I'm curious about Relucia, I like the twist about her being an Anguis, then yet the Military support them so in a bizarre way she's still on the same side. Twists and turns of backstabbing politics, very creative and complex and has lots of potential for future books. I want to know who that Anguis guy was at the end though.
I want to see Vis talk to Callidus' father, plus I'm curious to see how he talks to Ulciscor at the end, hopefully that's in the next book.
The trip to Suus was one of my favourite bits, so sad to see and a reflection on reality as it has brnr so common in history to destroy other cultures, it is so sad. I'm glad it's included as it shows so much what Is has lost and even snippits of life in Suus now. So good in a bad way. </spoiler>

Title: Die with Zero: Getting All You Can from Your Money and Your Life
Review:
An interesting finance book. Definitely a niche target audience, for higher earners and people who need the push to spend money, as most people save and invest too little. 
Some good tips about peak investment, what decades you want to have different experiences at and things like giving money to people/charities/etc. sooner and not as inheritance. 
Some things I don't necessarily agree with, you can absolutely spend more on retirement, especially if you pick up expensive hobbies (the amount of older people on extremely expensive cruises is increasing and definitely an option for easier travel when you may not be as healthy). Also given the target market will involve people retiring early, I'd expect a lot of people to spend at least as much if not more in retirement. 
Decent book, worth it to be a bit critical but it has some good ideas.

Title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
A Fate Inked In Blood
Review:
I've never been that interested in romantasy and I only read this as it's for my book club. It's definitely turned me off romantasy for good though. If it wasn't a book club read I probably would have DNF'd it. 
Aside from Freya and Bjorn, all the characters are a bit one dimensional, there aren't any arcs or growth for anyone aside from those two. 
Bjorn was a bit annoying but probably the best written character in the book, the only one with any sort of complexity. 
Freya I found so frustrating, she acts almost childlike, unable to do anything. I know the entire world is focused around men (which I also hate) but she could have broken free so many times and refuses. Everyone is awful, no idea why she is loyal to them. 
The plot is also kind of simple, it's easy to follow but it's pretty predictable, I guessed what would happen early on. I was hoping for more actual fantasy, at the start there was more, but it seemed to stop. It's frustrating as there were some concepts that could have been so much better and explored, there was so much potential but instead we got flat characters and no world building. 
I did skim some of the sex scenes as they didn't add anything to the plot. Good if you like smut, but not for me as it's sex for the sake of it, not relating to the story. I guess it's good if you like it but I find it hard to judge as it all seems so off and ridiculous to me. 
The writing is OK, the book is very readable, some phrases are overused but it's fine. What does annoy me is trying to make this a historical base and using terms that wouldn't exist back then, which an editor should have caught. 
Also I don't like books where there is such sexism when nobody even addresses it or tries to do anything about it. 
Overall I didn't like this book, but I guess I'm not the target audience as other people clearly like it. If you don't mind sexism, like smut, don't care about world building/fantasy and want more of a romance book that is easy to read I can see this being a good fit.

Title: A/S/L
Review:
I was hoping to like this book much more than I did.
I'm the exact market for this book, I got all the right nostalgia, I actually enjoyed the chat room pages and I code so nothing went over my head. 
I actually really enjoyed the start when they were kids much more than the rest of the book. The rest of it felt so slow, and there wasn't much character development either so it felt like nothing was happening. A lot of editing could have helped this, it could have been way shorter. 
I wish we saw more of Sash and Lilith and less of Abraxa. Her head was so hard to be in, it didn't make sense half the time and I just wanted to rush those chapters to go back to the other two. 
My last thing before spoilers, I got a bit confused as to when people were closeted or out as they never clarified and the correct pronouns and same names are always used. I figured out some of it, but I was really confused at some parts when I thought that characters were out when they weren't. Not sure how to fix it but it made it confusing, which probably didn't help as I was already confused and unsure about other parts of the book. 
One of my least favourite books in ages, very disappointing. 
<spoiler>For spoilers, I thought Lilith was out online as a kid but at the end it sounded like she wasn't and only Sash knew? I was very confused by this, as they used her name and pronouns correctly. Maybe as I'm not trans but something could have been clearer. 
About the ending, I was just a bit lost and kind of done with the book, no crying or any emotions at all really. I was sad they didn't all get together though, the entire book had been teasing it and nothing? Felt a bit let down by that. 
Abraxa going off had no closure which was sad, she had basically no character development, her chapters were hard to read and I didn't feel much about her story at all. I felt bad for everyone around her. 
I wanted Lilith to have a better story, her ending also seems a bit off (signing off and date seems ominous, though I'm not sure what it's the end of as not sure what spans those years, maybe her name?). I wish we heard more from her, I wanted her to do well at work and be happy but no. 
Sash I also wanted more from. Her ending also is up in the air, why no closure? My reaction to the ending is to reread to see if I'm missing something as it's barely an ending. 
I was rushing through the second half of the book as I wanted to get to the end and I was tempted to DNF, the ending barely made it worth it. </spoiler>

Title: Fourteen Days
Contributors: Emma Donoghue, Meg Wolitzer, Luis Alberto Urrea, Maria Hinojosa, Angie Cruz, Joseph Cassara, Roxana Robinson, Celeste Ng, Ishmael Reed, Tommy Orange, Diana Gabaldon, Pat Cummings, Tess Gerritsen, R.L. Stine, Mira Jacob, Monique Truong, Charlie Jane Anders, Erica Jong, Mary Pope Osborne, Scott Turow, John Grisham, James Shapiro, Dave Eggers, Nelly Rosario, C.J. Lyons, Sylvia Day, Caroline Randall Williams, Weike Wang, Jennine Capó Crucet, De'Shawn Charles Winslow, Nafissa Thompson-Spires, Rachel Vail, Alice Randall, Hampton Sides
Review:
It's a really interesting book, now that we're getting books about covid I like seeing different interpretations of it. 
It is a good amount of characters, the book does a good job reminding you who is who each time and focusing on a few so you don't loose track. 
It's very well put together, you may guess it is more than one author but nowhere near the number that are included, the editing is probably to thank for that. It can read as a short story collection, which is fine though not my personal favourite. I think it would have been nicer to have more parts about the characters together on the roof and less stories, as I cared about them far more than the stories themselves, some stories were great but others less so. 
I did really enjoy this book overall. 
<spoiler>
There is a twist at the end which I don't mind, but it could have come a bit earlier or the book could have been longer to explain it more as it was sudden and felt a bit like whiplash when you realised it. I would have preferred it to be explored a bit more. 
</spoiler>

Title: Kill Joy
Review:
I really enjoyed this. No idea why people rate it lower purely as it's a novella, I'm rating it based on that. 
It's a great little story. It gives you info on all the characters before the trilogy and it's a fun and quick read. 
It is nice how it ties into how Pip picks her EPQ as that isn't really covered in the main series and it works out well. 
Slight spoilers for the book below, but overall would definitely recommend this to anyone who likes the trilogy. 
<spoiler>I like how Pip came up with a better solution than the game. A bad designed game, or maybe one made stupidly easy, is reflective of the police doing the eays way out. Plus it's accurate, games can be badly designed. Pip should suggest an alternative ending to the company, hers was way better! 
Seeing Ravi at the end is great too.</spoiler>

Title: Half a World Away
Review:
I absolutely loved this book! It's a good read, completely unable to put it down once I started it. I was so invested in all of the characters and I was just rooting for them the entire time. 
It's a really well done how you flip between the two characters and the dichotomy of their lives, it really shows how much luck and privilege shapes how your life become. 
It's not a massive part of the story, but it's nice to have a good adoption, all the family seems happy, treated as just a normal thing rather than a plotline between birth vs adoptive family. 
The description 'emotionally high voltage' from the metro is very apt! More spoiler thoughts, but 5*.
<spoiler>
For Noah, I like how we learn more about him and see the mistakes he made, especially with his wife. He's a good Dad but not always a good husband, and you definitely don't blame Rosalind for everything. Taking your kid to a stranger's house without saying when you're separated definitely is not on! I can see why they come around at the end, with everything that happens, it is kind of realistic as they clearly do love each other. But I get her being so frustrated with him and like how it's handled. Millie didn't get brought up as much, but I liked her when she was. 
For Kerry and Kian, love their story. She's trying to be wonder woman and do everything and Kian seems to be your typical kid and I feel so much for everything he's going through. With Kerry going through treatment, she's such a trooper and I was holding out so much hope but Mike Gayle just loves to break my heart it seems, so many of his books do this too me! As soon as they started describing the hospice I instantly recognised it and knew what was happening. After the funeral I had to pause and go hug my partner as I was so upset, but it shows how much I cared about the characters. So sad but so good, amazing book. Now to read more of his books and break my heart again and again! </spoiler>

Title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
Contributors: Luke Poli (Narrator), Kristin Atherton (Narrator), Clare Corbett (Narrator), Jot Davies (Narrator), Olivia Forrest (Narrator)
Review:
I enjoyed this much more than I was expecting to! I saw this from the TV show but actually I enjoyed the book so much when I started watching the show it seemed so unfaithful I stopped. 
I was worried it would be too young adult for me as I don't read much anymore, but the characters are really well written, this feels like the kind of exceptional young adult I do still enjoy. Pip does do a few things that seem a bit stupid, but normal teenager levels of stupid. All the characters are well thought out, they all make sense in their decisions and I really like the overall cast - there are a lot of characters and they all fit in and have their place. 
The plot was really engaging and without spoilers, it's a good level of having twists and turns which are in keeping with the characters and what we know but it still has a level of unpredictability which is good in a mystery. 
Also I appreciate how British this book is, apparently there's an American version and I'm not sure how some of it translates but from EPQ to UCAS and the constant offering of tea I like it. I think more books should be reflective of their culture and not try to be too generic. So many British authors try to erase it to appeal to an international audience and I really appreciate that British culture has been kept here. 
Overall I really enjoyed this book, tv show doesn't seem great but I'm looking forward to the rest of the trilogy now!

Title: The Fault in Our Stars
Review: Amazing book. It is sad, yes, and will completely rip your heart out. But it is well written and you can't help but fall in love (or hate) with the characters. Even though it's not like most people's everyday life, it is still easy to relate to the characters which draws you into the book. It is a must-read.

Title: We Were Liars
Review:
It was a good book, maybe I'm just enjoying YA less than I used to but I didn't enjoy it as much as I thought I would. Not a bad book, I did still like it, just was expecting a bit more from it. 
<spoiler>
I didn't know much about this book going in, had no idea there was going to be a twist and I did enjoy it. I did get a bit annoyed at wishing people wood just talk to each other more, it did feel too convenient nobody would tell get anything. 
I know it us intentional, but sometimes I felt too annoyed at rich people problems and I wish the book handled it better. </spoiler>

Title: Fangirl
Review: Loved this story. A great light hearted read about characters going through changes of going away to university.

Title: Welcome to the Hyunam-dong Bookshop
Review:
I loved this book. It's great following the characters and learning more about their lives. It is a great cozy read and I'm always down for books about books. 
<spoiler>Also I really like books where characters don't follow traditional paths and potentially go against friends, family, etc. to follow what they want to do and I think this book does that really well. Not just with her opening the bookstore but also others throughout the book. It's OK to live the life you want and I appreciate that. The mix of it being a relaxing easy read scattered with not quite life lessons but things that make you think about what you really want is well balanced.</spoiler>

Title: Four Seasons in Japan
Review:
This was a fun easy book to read. The characters are interesting, though I prefer Kyo and Ayako story to Flo's.
I really like the dynamic between the two of them, how they both grow and learn because of each other, it is like a cultural exchange between generations which I found really interesting. I didn't like Ayako a lot of the time, but not every character had to be likeable and a grandmother acting that way is unfortunately quite realistic. More thoughts in spoilers below! 
Flo was OK but we didn't get enough of her story to care about her as much and I just found her parts a bit boring and repetitive, nothing in her story paid off at all. If her parts were omitted the story may have even been better. Again, more spoiler thoughts below.
Overall I did enjoy it, but I prefer it for the story inside which is a nice story and not trying to be something deeper.
<spoiler>I love Ayako and Kyo. All their family history is fascinating, I like learning about Onomichi and everyone in the village too. The moi tain stories are great and I like learning bits and pieces throughout the book. Also it's odd about Kyo's Mum, wish Ayako stood up for him but she's a stereotypical workaholic pushing Kyo to be as well. 
Flo has no payoff, nothing comes out of the ex-girlfriend or her friends, she is flailing with no direction and doesn't grow or change for the entire story and there is no closure. Things like the book her ex wrote could have been relevant in the end but no.
The book in a book concept is fun but it's been done better before. That part of the book is unnecessary for me, the best part is Kyo and Ayako, they are the heart of this story and it doesn't need extra wrapping, I honestly think it may have been better without it. It felt like when someone is trying to add extra stuff to overcompensate, but the characters are good and the story didn't need the extra fluff in my opinion. </spoiler>

Title: A Darker Shade of Magic
Review:
A really fun fantasy book to read. It's nice to read a shorter fantasy book and look forward to the next books too.
The characters are interesting, flawed but not too much so. 
The plot took a while to start, but I did enjoy learning about the world initially instead as I find it a really cool idea with how the different Londons work. 
Only slight complaint is it did feel a bit YA/simpler than other fantasy books, though my brain needs a break from those so this was good for that. 
Overall a good fun fantasy book, no major complaints, can't wait to finish the series. 
<spoiler>
I liked Lila's journey, from a selfish thief to someone willing to give their life for something good. She was a great character to follow. 
Also with Kell, hopefully he learns some lessons from this. 
I want to know more on both their back stories, we don't know much about either of them and I was hoping we'd learn more. Maybe it will be explored more in future books. Generally I liked the plot but it started quite late in the book with the stone. It wasn't clear at first what the overall plot would be, but I wanted to read anyway to learn more about the characters. 
I wish we'd actually got to black London and not just ended with white London. Again, maybe future books. 
</spoiler>

Title: Bringing Down the Flowers
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. I was worried it would be too depressing, given the subject matter, but I read it far quicker than I expected too.
I was really rooting for Cedar the entire time, and all the women of the world, hoping that they could overturn some of the insane laws that are in place. 
The concept is interesting and executed well, all the background characters are done well and have their own thoughts and lives which I like. 
As someone who lives in Birmingham, it's great to hear about different places and how they've changed. Nice to not have London be the capital! I want to find more books based in Birmingham and this is a great one, even if it's not the best version of Birmingham in the future. 
The plot is good, more notes in spoilers below. 
Only downside is I need another book and there isn't one (yet)! 
<spoiler>I like how while this is a dystopia type novel, it seems that there actually may be a way out of it unlike a lot of others. I want more books like this! 
Loved how the different characters weave in and out of the story, like how Ms Bayley turns up again and the doctor you meet randomly turns out to be a major character later on.
I appreciate that they do note the world is bad for men too, mainly fertile men, but it is worse for women. It needs to change for everyone!
My only criticism is I wish at the end while she did find her son, we don't know about if she needs to have more kids or not. I'm assuming not given the six months later but it wasn't clear. 
Also it does suffer a bit from feeling like the first book in a series, I'm assuming there will be more books but none are out yet. 
I need to know more! </spoiler>

Title: Lessons in Chemistry
Review:
I put this book as OK. I liked bits and disliked others. I am glad I finished it but I wouldn't recommend it, especially not to women in science. I would compare it to something like The Big Bang Theory, the mass audience may like it but lots of people dislike the representation and find bits problematic. I would definitely not class this book as historical fiction either, it doesn't reflect the time period at all. 

<spoiler>
I have a few things I dislike, some small things like the talking dog and impossibly smart child make this book more like fantasy. From converting a kitchen into a lab at home, becoming a rower from textbooks, making the perfect coffee even coffee haters would love and better food than any house wife. It seemed like she was perfect in every way. 
I saw another review say it is like someone from the 2020s was sent back in time, which is accurate, it really doesn't read accurate for the time period, it makes no sense. Also the science is all wrong but that's often the case with these books so I wasn't expecting as much there, but referencing things from the future was a bit much. In a similar vain, a chemist learning physics (different disciplines!) and becoming an amazing rower from a book seems unrealistic too. Though aside from the learning, the rowing part of the book seemed more well thought out and researched than any of the science. 
It was very odd that she would refuse to call salt anything but NaCl, scientists do usually use normal words outside the lab, it was like she was being quirky but it made no sense. Which made what I think is the worst line in the book even more stupid, she claimed canned soup is 'bad because it's full of chemicals' when she calls every component by it's chemical name. Sounded like a crunchy mum from today, so out of place in this setting. 
I felt the sexual assault wasn't handled very well. I appreciate all the sexism and like how some of that was handled, but she never had any trauma or thinks back on any of the sexual assault so I'm not really sure why it's there. 
Overall I think this book could be good which is why it frustrates me. A better editor (including scientific and historic accuracy), maybe moving it to the 90s would make it seem a bit more realistic. If it stuck more to a light hearted chemist becomes tv cook. It seemed to try to be both that and a more serious tale on feminism from the 50s. It did the former much better than the latter and I wish it stuck more to that instead. 
</spoiler>

Title: Everything is Tuberculosis
Review:
A great book all about tuberculosis. Not really much to add, it's very informative, sad, but a really insightful look into why the disease is still so prevelent today despite being curable.
I'm not usually one for non fiction but I really enjoyed this book despite that.

Title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
Review:
The book was alright, I enjoyed reading some of it but a few things bugged me when reading it. 

<spoiler>
I think you're supposed to like Sadie but I found her so unlikeable. It wild be fine if it was intentional but everyone seems to love her and I can't figure out why. 
Also as a women in the tech industry, it made me so mad to see this depiction of women being shown as awful, unsupportive of each other and having unprofessional relationships which is really sad to see. I was hoping for a more inspiring book about women in stem, not this. 
Also the entire relationship with Dov and Sadie is so unprofessional from the start, feeds into a horrible stereotype about women sleeping their way up in stem careers. Also it is clearly abusive but tries to make light of it and make Dov seem like a good person anyway which was awful. Having abuse can work in a story, but not if you're making excuses for abusers.
Overall I did enjoy parts of the book, but couldn't give more than a 3*for it given the issues. </spoiler>

Title: Dengue Boy
Review:
I don't know hit to describe this book or what even to think of it. It is very bizarre and experimental.
I get what it's going for but I think it's a bit much in some places. There are so many different concepts and ideas, it felt like it could have been a longer book as it's pretty short and some things could have been delved into a bit more. Some points did feel like shock value just for the sake of it which I wasn't a fan of. 
Also I would advise reading this book over a short period time as when I came back to it I was a little lost at first as so much was going on. 
<spoiler>I liked things like virofinance, the video game section and how the different classes live. The end felt a bit confusing though with weird time travel and what is a video game vs reality, I was a little lost. I needed more.l explanation.
The sexual stuff felt so unnecessaryi didn't get why so much was included. I got that everyone liked to rape the sheepies all the time the first time which I didn't like, and the repetition of it was pointless. One of the things that felt like it was put in for shock value as it added nothing else. </spoiler>
I'm glad I read it, it's note really my taste but it's good to read outside your comfort zone. I'd struggle to recommend it to a lot of people though.

Title: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader
Homegoing
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. I wasn't sure exactly what to expect going in but I'm so glad I read it.
It is very hard to read at first, it gets a bit easier but I'd advise checking trigger warnings as a lot are checked off for this book. 
It reads like short stories, following snippets of lives of each generation over a few hundred years. It's amazin how different and the same some stories are. Most of them are heartbreaking and a lot of the characters don't have great lives, but it does seem to get a bit better as it goes on. 
The family tree at the start of the book is useful, but don't look back on it mid story as it spoils who gets married for some of the stories. 
I would say this is a must read for learning a bit more about history that is not often taught or talked about. Whilst it's fiction, you know a lot of people have lived similar lives and it's good to remember our history. 
<spoiler>A few spoiler thoughts. I know it is true and part of the history, but there is so much rape and sexual assault I found it hard to get through parts. I know it's valid and part of the story but it's just not something I like to read really. There is a lot of violence as well, it is not an easy read. 
A few of the stories felt like they didn't fully end, I think Abena's especially felt like we didn't know she went to the monistery and Sonny's, both of which the kids weren't born which felt missing. 
The ending was good, I like the fears if water and fire together there. I was hoping they'd realise they were related or that they find the other stone, I know it's not the most realistic but it is a book after all! I don't get why she gave away the necklace to him without knowing they were related, that felt a little odd.
Loved the book overall though! 
</spoiler>
Content Warnings: Graphic: Death, Physical abuse, Racial slurs, Racism, Rape, Sexual assault, Sexual violence, Slavery, Torture, Violence, Trafficking, Murder, Sexual harassment, Colonisation, War, Deportation; Moderate: Child death, Drug abuse, Drug use, Hate crime, Violence, Blood, Grief, Death of parent, Fire/Fire injury, Abandonment, War;

Title: My Brilliant Friend
Review:
It was a bit slow to get into, but I found it picked up as it went along. The second half of the book I read in a day as I wanted to finish it.
I found it really interesting learning about all the different characters in their home area, though I really don't like many of them. 
This book is really well written and explores all the characters very well, making you love and hate different people. One line can completely make you do a 180 in how you feel about someone.
I like Lena's ability in school, it shows that women have always been academic, even if they've not always been given the credit they are due in the past, especially as shown with Lila. It really shows how having supportive adults around you can completely change the course of your life. 
Only knocking off a star as it didn't engage me straight away and I wasn't completely wowed by it, but I'll definitely be reading the rest of these books - though I may need a bit of a break as it isn't exactly an easy read. 
<spoiler>A few extra spoiler thoughts, I like how the girls are smarter than the boys, both Lila and Lena. Just a small thing I liked.
Not sure how I feel about that last bit at the end with the evil Marcello not only showing up to the wedding but wearing the special shoes Lila made, which Stefano bought. Mean cliff hanger, do I now hate Stefano too? He seemed like one of the few decent guys in the book. I need a break before book two but also I want to know now! Not a massive fan of endings like that, I'd have rather it was the beginning of the next book instead.</spoiler>

Title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
The Midnight Library
Review:
I really enjoyed this book. I'd heard good things but send mixed reviews so went into it unsure.
I loved the entire book, I couldn't put it down once I'd started it. There is a bit of plot but it's more about the main character. 
It isn't necessarily ground breaking, but it's a fun concept and was executed really well. 
Giving it a 4.5 star as I loved it. I know there are some more complex issues with mental health and such, but it didn't prevent my enjoyment at the time (though looking back I can see some issues) so only knocking off half a star for it. 
<spoiler>
I loved all the different variations of her life, it makes you reflect on your life too and I was wondering what my alternative lives would be. 
I was hoping she'd come back to the initial one at the end and I'm really glad she did.</spoiler>

Title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
Heartstopper Volume 2
Review:
A really fun read. The pictures and dialog really show how characters are feeling and make you laugh out loud, be angry and root for them. 
Great representation too.

Title: Girls Under Pressure
Review:
Nice lighthearted book. It goes over topics like dieting, relationships, etc. in an accessible way without being too heavy.
Great for a book for teens, and a nice nostalgia read for adults!

Title: Great Big Beautiful Life
Review:
I generally liked this book. The chapters vary between Margaret's story and the romance plot, I definitely found Margaret's stuff much more interesting, that's what I enjoyed most from this story.
The romance was fine, Hayden felt a bit flat compared to other characters, I wish we had learnt a bit more about him. 
If you want romance, I'm not sure if this is the best choice as the story with Margaret plays more of a role and is more fleshed out than the romance, which is very predictable and not too exciting. Personally I much prefer the story with Margaret and wish some of the romance was scrapped to flesh out more of the story. 
Overall I enjoyed it, it's a nice easy light read. Nothing groundbreaking but still a good time. 
<spoiler>I liked the twist at the end with Hayden's Mum, wasn't expecting it, unlike most of the twists in these kind of books. 
What I was expecting is them to do the book together, which also happened, a bit too predictable.
Also a side note, the pregnancy at the end was pointless, I hate how so often people add in marriage or a baby to signify a happy ending, I wish that had been excluded and they were focused on their careers instead. Couldn't it have ended with the two of them embarking on their Great Big Beautiful life? </spoiler>

Title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
A Story for Every Day of Spring
Review:
A good collection overall, some better than others though, a few not so great and a few outstanding ones.
A good way to get back into reading too if you want of read one or two pages a day.

Title: The Callista Alignment
Review:
A really interesting book, more plot based and I liked following the characters, I was rooting for them the entire. 
Very sci-fi and I don't always like sci-fi, but I enjoyed it in this case and I think it was really well done. 
It's interesting to see how humans are treated and makes you think about how we treat animals and such which I enjoy. 
It did feel a bit like the first book in a series or wider universe, which isn't all bad, but there was a lot of setup and things left in a way for potential future books, which could have focused more on this book than hypothetical future books.

Title: Days at the Morisaki Bookshop
Review:
I nice fun read. Anything book related is always a plus for me.
Nothing overly negative, aside from a few spoilers below, but nothing particularly wowed me or stood out either. A good read, but nothing that memorable. 
<spoiler>
A few specifics, I liked the main character and the Uncle, their relationship was really good. Wasn't a fan of his relationship with his wife though, it felt really unhealthy, and the way it was written it was like you were supposed to root for them but I couldn't. 
It was an odd mix of character and plot, I wish there was more focus on either as it felt a bit like they both could use more - it wasn't bad, I just needed more of it. It almost felt incomplete. I know it's more slice of life but we could have used more to fill in some of the gaps. The book is so short, it wouldn't be an issue to add more to it. 
The first half was much better, I didn't care about the Aunt as much and would have preferred to go more in depth with the other relationships instead of introducing her. 
I did enjoy it though and may read the sequel some day, but I'm not rushing out for it. 
</spoiler>

Title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
Charm Quest
Review: Another good entry to the series, without saying any spoilers it's sadder and more infuriating than some of the others. Well written but I get so annoyed at some characters but it's a a testament to how we some of them have been built up over the series.

Title: Wild Boar
Review:
This was a really interesting book that I'm finding it really hard to review.
I enjoyed reading it. The writing was very good, kudos to the translator as well as the author for this. It was well written in a way that didn't make me feel dumb like sometimes literary books do. 
The characters are a mixture. Ritve was my favourite, loved all their sections. Their story made sense and I liked how it played out. Glenn was also good but just a bit less interesting to me. Mia lost me a bit, the Grandfather stuff was so confusing at the end I couldn't make heads or tails of some of the events and what was actually happening. Won't say spoilers, maybe I'm being silly and missing something, but this one confused me. 
Also part of another ending threw me off a bit too, no spoilers but it felt jarring and then just moved on and I was left unsure if what I thought happened really happened. 
I did really enjoy the vibe of the book. I like how it describes the world and how the boars affect different people. We don't see much of them, just the impact they have on the world. Also reading it whilst in a train travelling through Sweden makes it better too! 
Overall I think I'd recommend it, it's a short book and not too difficult to read and despite a few hangups I did really enjoy it.

Title: How to Kill Men and Get Away With It
Tiny Moons: A Year of Eating in Shanghai
Review: I loved this book. I probably read it too quickly as I couldn't put it down. The only negative is that it isn't the most memorable of books, I'm not sure it will be one I'll look back on in the future. I enjoyed every second I spent reading it though and maybe on the flipside it will be a good reread.

Title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
The Girl in The Tower
Review:
I enjoyed this book, a similar amount to the first. 
I liked following Vasya more as an adult now and seeing how her story unfolds in the world, a blend of historic and fantasy which I found really interesting. 
Despite being the second book it was a story by itself, the first book being necessary background, but there is a solid beginning, middle and end which I was happy about. You wouldn't know there is a book after it, but of course I'm going to have to read it now. 
I liked it a similar amount to the first book overall. 
<spoiler>I liked following Sasha more this book, I'm glad to see more of him than we did in turn first book. Her sister Olga is just a sad story, I really hope Marya has a better upbringing but I'm worried for her. I like there being one women per generation who can see the cheryti. 
Dmitrii is an odd character, it's weird how the sexism is so stark, but I guess it is of the time. I'm just glad there is much less rape in this book. 
I found Morozko's weird love but not relationship with Vasya a bit odd, I would have liked a bit more to it and I doubt we'll see him again. 
Konstantin I hate even more and when Vasya said she'd kill him if she saw him again I hope she does, or he goes away and never returns. 
Also the ghost woman in the tower could have used a bit more, the link to Kasyan makes sense but not sure why she haunted Vaysa and especially Mayra so much. 
Those are my random spoiler. Thoughts, a mix of good and improvements but mostly good. </spoiler>

Title: Girls In Tears
Review:
Reading all the series before think again. 
A nice fun nostalgia read, though got annoyed at the end <spoiler>with her giving Russel another chance, he so doesn't deserve it</spoiler>. 
Otherwise a nice book about friendship and the mistakes teens make.

Title: Good Girl, Bad Blood
Contributors: Kristin Atherton (Narrator), Luke Poli (Narrator), Claire Corbett (Narrator), Jot Davies (Narrator), Richard Hughes (Narrator), Mariam Grace (Narrator)
Review:
This was a really good book to read. I needed something easy and engaging and this definitely fit the bill. 
I like how it leads on from the first book and it is a good way of drawing Pip back in, as she's originally trying to avoid detective work again. 
I like how the twists and turns happened throughout the Story. Without being too spoiler I think it had  maybe a bit too much deviation from the original issue than I would have liked, as it went from one case to another, but I did like the ending to the story, it felt like a satisfying conclusion. 
Not quite as good as the first book, but still a really good book.

Title: The Song of Achilles
Review:
I really liked this book. It's a bit slow to start, I couldn't really get into it so put it down for a while. But when I picked it up again a few weeks later it only took me two days to finish as I was hooked!
I really like the point of view of Patroclus for this story and how he sees Achilles. He loves him and thinks he can do no wrong, even when he clearly is to the reader, which I like . The prose of the entire book is lovely to, easy to read yet still well written with some brilliant quotes you can look pull out.
A few minor things I didn't like, the aging isn't always clear, they age a lot and it isn't obvious how much time passes sometimes. In line with this, the character of Achilles does change dramatically from the child/teen learning music to the warrior without a lot of buildup so it seems sudden.
Also it would be nice if sexuality was a bit less binary, let bisexuality exist please. 
Overall though would recommend it, only a few minor complaints to an otherwise great novel.

Title: Relic Quest
Review: Love this book and all the quest series.

Title: DallerGut Dream Department Store
Contributors: Sandy Joosun Lee (Translator), Thyrze van Onna (Translator)
Review:
I really enjoyed reading this. I liked following Penny, her journey learning about the store and being introduced to all the other characters you meet throughout the story. I wish we had more time with some of them though. 
I read this over a long period of time and it's easy to dip in and out of. 
The concept is great and I can't wait to read the sequel. 
<spoiler>My only minor complaint is that it's a weird mix of character and plot, I kind of wish it leaned a bit further in one direction, but I still enjoyed it and will definitely be reading the sequel.</spoiler>

Title: The Parsley Bed
Review:
Loved the first book and the second in the series doesn't disappoint!
Glad to be following Cedar again, though the world is as awful as ever. It's hard to review without spoilers, but I'd say if you liked the first book I would a hundred percent recommend this too. I think I still prefer the first book but this book is pretty close behind. 
I like how the different characters all develop and learning more about the law and science party is interesting. More thoughts in spoilers, so I'll just say I liked it, the plot as a whole and the way it ended. It wraps the current situation up mostly and is a nice way of making it so I want to read more but don't feel like it's left on a cliffhanger for the next book. Very well done! 
So glad I read it, sad now I have to wait so long for the next one! 
<spoiler>Spoiler time!
I like learning more and more about Stern, I really hope to see more of him and I'll be sad if we don't next book. I hope he gets out without becoming a forced sperm donar. 
The surprise of the rise in fertility I didn't see coming, some of it is left hanging a bit with the boys being let go and nothing much coming of it but I hope we learn more of it next book. I feel for Frankie and Diya, wish we got more of a wrapup there. Same with her mother and Ms Sadie, no idea what will happen to them, I need to know! 
Cedar being pregnant I guess I shouldn't be surprised at, I guess herbal contraception isn't flawless in this world, I'm glad she got to keep her baby though given all the past issues. I like the hope little Juniper will be able to maybe meet her siblings one day. 
Not necessary a critism, but I do hope we hear more from people who are childfree in this world. There hasn't been any focus on it and it seems like a good opportunity, how childfree women try to avoid the ceremonies, back alley sterilisation, there could be so much to explore it feels like a missed opportunity right now. The series isn't over yet though so I live in hope! 
Overall great book though, loved it. </spoiler>

Title: The Thousand-Dollar Tan Line
Review:
A good solid book. I would recommend it to anyone who is a fan of Veronica Mars, and while you could read it without having watched the show and movie I would advise watching them first. 
A great mystery, I liked following Veronica after the movie left off here. The relationship between her and her Dad is great, though I do find it jarring when he's referred to as Keith. 
<spoiler>The only thing I wasn't a massive fan of is Mac working for her and not at Kane anymore, it felt a bit too contrived. Even if she left Kane or still consulted for Veronica sometimes, I'd expect her to have some other form of income, like being self employed or part of some cool start-up.
I really enjoyed the book, the ending felt satisfying and was a good in between of not being predictable but still believable and it made sense. I'm not sure how I feel about Lianne being around, but the full circle at the end with her being abandoned was great so I'll forgive it feeling a bit forced earlier. </spoiler>

Title: You Are Here
Review:
Overall I enjoyed this book. It's a fun read, definitely about the characters rather than plot. You learn so much about everyone, especially Michael and Marnie. Those two are really interesting to follow, I especially like the parts where they discuss the same thing in such different ways, it gives you an insight into how they see the world. 
The side characters often felt a bit one note, they aren't really the focus, but some really didn't add a lot. 
More spoiler thoughts below, but generally a good read. Nothing ground breaking but I'm glad I read it. 
<spoiler>Like a walk, I'd say this book is about the journey and not the ending. The journey is interesting, exploring more and more about the characters. There is a lot of will they won't they, a little too much at points but not by much. Some parts were really well done, like handling Michael's infertility. The kid felt a little pointless to include and Connor only seemed there to be Michael's opposite. 
I liked the walk much more than the bits after it, I was pushing through to the end. Learning about random dates here and there, I did not care about the amazing Tessa, I just wanted to know about Michael and Marnie. The end was a bit of a let down in that way, I wanted more about them and not others. I did like the end feels like a new beginning though, just wished we could see a bit more of it. </spoiler>

Title: Daisy Jones & The Six
Review:
I really enjoyed reading this book.
I like stories semi based on real life and this is right up my alley. The format is really interesting and engaged me immediately, I'd love to read more books written in this style. 
Overall, a great book and I'd definitely recommend it. 

<spoiler>
I loved following the band, all the members were different and hearing all their perspectives was a good way of telling the story. 
I also love Karen's story specifically, it's really great to show a woman who doesn't want the traditional marriage and kids and doesn't change her mind. It's really underrepresented in media and I really appreciate it here. 
I know some may not be happy with the band breaking up or the way some things happened, but it seems very realistic and I thought it was well written. 
My only minor complaint is the reveal of the author didn't feel like a big deal, it probably could have been done better, it didn't really add anything to the story.</spoiler>

Title: The Trees
Review:
I enjoyed this book overall but had a few issues with it.
